name: haxfinity
desc:
HAXFINITY — Hack the Infinite

The 24-hour hackathon of XTHRON '26

 December 2026
Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala
Prize Pool: Exciting prizes
Team Size: 2–4 participants

Build real solutions. Solve meaningful problems. Create something that works.

HAXFINITY is the 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON '26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur.

For 24 hours, students from different colleges and backgrounds will come together to identify problems, develop solutions, build working prototypes, and present their ideas to a panel of judges.

There is no compulsory theme. Participants are free to choose a problem and develop a solution using any suitable technology.

Whether you are an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, HAXFINITY is a space to learn, collaborate, experiment, and build.

PRIZE POOL — Exciting prizes


TRACKS

OPEN INNOVATION

Build anything that solves a real problem.

You may work in education, healthcare, finance, agriculture, entertainment, productivity, cybersecurity, accessibility, sustainability, or any other domain.

There is no fixed problem statement and no restriction on technology. Choose a problem, design a solution, build a working prototype, and surprise the judges.

AI / ML

Build intelligent systems using machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, recommendation systems, data analysis, or any other AI-related technology.

Projects will be evaluated on technical implementation, originality, usefulness, and real-world applicability.

SOCIAL GOOD

Build technology that improves people’s lives.

Possible areas include rural development, accessibility, mental health, financial inclusion, education, healthcare, environmental protection, and community welfare.

Projects in this track will be evaluated on impact, usability, sustainability, and the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

WHAT THE HACKATHON LOOKS LIKE

16 December, 10:30 AM — Opening ceremony and problem-solving begins.

During the day — Teams form, ideas take shape, and development begins.

Throughout the event — Mentoring, technical support, checkpoints, and interaction with fellow participants.

Midnight — The hackathon continues with snacks, discussions, debugging, and late-night building.

17 December, 10:32 AM — Submission deadline and code freeze.

After submission — Teams prepare their final demonstrations.

Final judging — Each team presents its working prototype to the judges.

Closing ceremony — Winners are announced and prizes are distributed.

WHO CAN PARTICIPATE?

HAXFINITY is open to students from all streams and colleges.

Students from computer science, information technology, engineering, science, commerce, management, design, and other disciplines are welcome.

You may participate if you are:

- A beginner attending your first hackathon.
- An experienced developer.
- A designer or creative problem-solver.
- A student interested in AI, cybersecurity, cloud, robotics, web, mobile, or social-impact technology.
- Someone with an idea and the willingness to build it.

The only requirement is that you come prepared to learn, collaborate, and create.

TEAM DETAILS

- Each team must have 2–4 participants.
- Solo participation is not permitted.
- Participants from different colleges may form one team.
- Participants from different academic streams may form one team.
- Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.
- Each participant may be part of only one team.

WHERE IT HAPPENS

Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)
Santhigramam, Eranhimangad
Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329

The campus is located in the Nilambur region of Kerala, known for its natural surroundings and teak forests.

The college is approximately:

- 3 km from Nilambur Railway Station.
- 1 km from the Calicut–Nilambur–Ooty highway.

Travel and accommodation information will be shared with registered participants.

WHAT WE PROVIDE

- Dedicated workspace for participating teams.
- Power and internet access.
- Lunch on the first day.
- Dinner on the first day.
- Breakfast on the second day.
- Midnight snacks.
- Technical assistance during the event.
- Mentoring and guidance, subject to mentor availability.
- Certificates for participants.
- A platform to demonstrate projects to judges and fellow innovators.

Cloud credits, software benefits, and additional resources may be announced later if they are officially confirmed.

RULES

- Teams must contain 2–4 participants.
- The project must be developed during the official hackathon period.
- Participants may use open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and publicly available datasets.
- Previously developed projects may not be submitted as new work.
- Teams must clearly disclose any pre-existing code, templates, datasets, APIs, or third-party services used.
- Projects must be submitted through Devfolio before the deadline.
- Late submissions may not be accepted.
- A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected.
- Teams must be prepared to explain their technology, development process, and contribution.
- Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law.
- All participants must follow the event Code of Conduct.
- The organisers reserve the right to reject projects that are unsafe, copied, offensive, illegal, or unrelated to the event.
- The detailed judging criteria and final rules will be published before the event.




HAXFINITY — Hack the Infinite
EXTHRONE ’26
12–13 December 2026
location: Amal College of Advanced Studies, Nilambur, Myladi, Eranhimangad, Kerala, India

name: Hefty-Hacks
tagline: Code the Markets. Build the Future of Finance.
desc:
# ⚡ Hefty Hacks

**Hefty Hacks** is a fully-online **Finance × Trading** hackathon presented by **TechZap**. Over one intense sprint, engineers, quants and designers turn market chaos into working product — trading systems, market predictors, fintech, risk engines, DeFi and everything in between.

Pick a niche. Go absurdly deep. Ship something the street hasn't seen yet.

> 🌟 **Exclusive Career Opportunity**: The **Top 10 teams** will get a chance to participate in direct hiring rounds with leading companies and fast-growing startups. 
> 
> *(Selection for interviews and hiring is solely at the discretion of the participating companies and subject to their individual eligibility criteria and recruitment policies.)*

> **Finance. Trading. Innovation.** — one laptop, a thesis worth defending, and 36 hours to prove it.

---

## 🚀 What is Hefty Hacks?

The markets never sleep, and neither do great builders. Hefty Hacks challenges you to build at the intersection of **finance and trading** — from high-frequency execution engines to market predictors, robo-advisors, fraud radars and on-chain quant tooling.

There's one rule that decides winners: **go narrow.** Anyone can build "a trading app." The teams that win pick a niche so specific it sounds obsessive — then own it.

- 🌐 **100% Online** — hack from anywhere in the world
- 👥 **Teams of 2–6** — no solo entries; finance is a team sport
- 🗓️ **Final Hack Day: 31 Oct – 1 Nov** — a 36-hour build sprint
- 🏆 **₹75,000 prize pool** + free Azure credits + elite mentorship

---

## 🎯 Tracks

Build on either track — or fuse them into something nobody has shipped yet.

### 01 · Finance
Reinvent how money moves, grows and stays safe — on-chain or off.
- Payments, lending & neo-banking
- Personal finance & wealth autopilot
- Fraud, AML & risk intelligence
- Insurance, credit scoring & RegTech
- **Decentralized finance (DeFi)** — on-chain lending, tokenization & protocols

### 02 · Trading
Turn market microstructure into a working edge.
- Algo, HFT & execution engines
- Futures, options & derivatives tooling
- Market prediction & alt-data signals
- Backtesting & portfolio optimization

### 03 · Fusion *(the boldest bets score highest)*
Combine both tracks into something genuinely unique.
- Sentiment-to-signal fintech apps
- On-chain quant & DeFi execution
- Embedded trading inside consumer finance
- Your own uncharted crossover

---

## 🤖 On Using AI

**Bring the idea. Let AI sharpen it.**

Generating your idea straight from an AI is **strongly discouraged** — judges can smell a generated pitch, and a borrowed thesis has no conviction behind it. Instead:

1. Pick a niche narrow enough to defend in one sentence.
2. Write your **own** thesis first — the bet nobody else is making.
3. Use AI to attack it: what breaks, what's been tried, what's missing.
4. Refine, prototype, and ship the version only your team could build.

**Your niche, AI's leverage.** Originality is the edge we score for.

---

## ⚖️ How We Judge

- **Originality of the niche** — how sharp and defensible is the bet?
- **Technical depth** — did you actually build the hard part?
- **Working demo** — does it run and hold up under questions?
- **Market insight** — do you understand the problem you're solving?

A sharp, unique idea executed well beats a broad idea half-built.

---

## 🛠️ Presented by TechZap

Hefty Hacks is built and run by **TechZap** — bringing builders together to disrupt finance.

**Build. Innovate. Disrupt.**
---

name: QuantHacks
desc:
# QuantHacks

## Code. Quantify. Innovate.

**QuantHacks** is a hackathon organized by the **London Institute of Actuarial Studies (LIAS)**, bringing together technology, data, and actuarial science to tackle real-world problems involving **risk, uncertainty, and decision-making**.

From cybersecurity and financial technology to education and career development, participants are challenged to build practical solutions using **artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, probability, and predictive analytics**.

The goal isn't simply to build another application. It's to use **quantitative thinking and technology to understand uncertainty, predict outcomes, and make better decisions.**

### 🚀 What Can You Build?

Participants can explore three core tracks:

* 🛡️ **Cybersecurity**
  Quantify cyber risk, predict potential incidents, estimate financial losses, or build smarter risk assessment systems.

* 💰 **FinTech**
  Build solutions for credit risk, financial planning, insurance pricing, loan defaults, investment decisions, or financial forecasting.

* 🎓 **EdTech**
  Apply predictive analytics to student performance, exam preparation, dropout risk, personalized learning, and career planning.

### 📊 The Quantitative Edge

Every project should meaningfully incorporate **actuarial or quantitative principles**, such as:

* Probability and statistical modeling
* Risk assessment
* Predictive analytics
* Expected value and expected loss
* Frequency and severity modeling
* Machine learning
* Scenario and stress testing
* Monte Carlo simulation
* Data-driven decision making

You don't need to build a complicated mathematical model just for the sake of it. The objective is to show how quantitative reasoning **actually improves your solution**.

### 🏆 The Challenge

**Can you turn uncertainty into an advantage?**

Bring your ideas, your code, and your curiosity. Build something useful, back your decisions with data, and show us what happens when **technology meets the mathematics of risk.**

**QuantHacks — Code. Quantify. Innovate.**

name: The Great Agent Hackathon
desc:
**The Great Agent Hackathon, presented by TGPF 2026**

The Great Agent Hackathon is a 24-hour, in-person build happening overnight in Bangalore, as part of The Great Product Festival, India's largest product and startup conference.

Teams get real problem statements, real mentorship through the night, and a live Main Stage finale in front of India's top product leaders at TGPF.

This year's hackathon is powered by Freshworks as title sponsor, with ElevenLabs powering the build.

**Problem Statement Tracks**

**• Track 1 — Customer Experience & Employee Onboarding:** agents built on Freshworks Agent Studio, MCP, and multi-agent orchestration.

**• Track 2 — Platform Agent Skills & Knowledge:** reusable skills, MCP integrations, and the Freshworks developer platform.

**• Track 3 — AI-native Enterprise (Open):** open canvas, any stack, greenfield agentic products.

**Requirements**

***Stage 1: Online Qualification Round***
To qualify for The Great Agent Hackathon, teams must submit the following on Devpost before the qualification deadline:

1. **A Figma prototype or working demo** of your idea addressing one of the 3 problem statement tracks. This does not need to be a finished product, a clickable prototype, wireframe flow, or early build is enough to show the idea clearly.

2. **A short written submission** covering:

(i). The problem statement your team is addressing
(ii). Your proposed solution and how it works
(iii). Why your team is the right one to build it

3. **A brief video walkthrough** (1-2 minutes) explaining your prototype and idea. Loom, YouTube, or Vimeo links are fine.
4. **Team details:** names, roles, and one line on relevant experience for each team member.

Submissions will be reviewed by the TGPF and sponsor team. Shortlisted teams will be notified and invited to Bangalore for the in-person build.

 

**Stage 2: In-Person Build (Bangalore, Shortlisted Teams Only)**
Shortlisted teams travel to Bangalore for the 24-hour overnight build as part of TGPF 2026.

At this stage, teams must submit:

1. **A working prototype or demo** of the product built during the 24-hour build window, functional and ready to demo live.

2. **An updated project description** covering what was built, the tech stack used, and how it evolved from the original Stage 1 idea.

3. **Public code repository link** (GitHub or equivalent) with a clear README.

4. **A live demo** on the Main Stage in front of judges and the TGPF audience.

**Judging Criteria**

**Innovation & Originality**
How creative and original is the idea? Does it approach the problem statement in a way we haven't seen before, or push beyond an obvious solution?

**Technical Execution**
How well is the project built? Judges will look at functionality, code quality, and whether the team pulled off what they set out to build within the time given.

**Use of AI / Agentic Design**
Does the project meaningfully use AI or agent-based workflows to solve the problem, rather than bolting AI on as an afterthought?

**Relevance to Problem Statement**
How directly does the solution address the chosen track, Tech in Product, Growth and Monetisation, Sponsor-Driven Challenge, or Open Track, and how well does it solve a real, clearly defined problem?

**Presentation & Demo Quality**
How clearly does the team communicate what they built, why it matters, and how it works during the live demo? Judges will weigh clarity and storytelling, not just polish.

**Potential Impact**
If this were taken further, how much real-world value could it create for the people or businesses it's meant to serve?

* Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and respect towards fellow participants, mentors, judges, and organizers.

name: FusioniX2026
desc:
# **FusioniX 2026**
**Overview**

FusioniX 2026 is a 24-hour national-level hybrid Offline hackathon organized by the Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering and the Department of Computer Science & Engineering (IoT), University of Engineering and Management, Kolkata.

FusioniX focuses on solving real-world engineering challenges by combining hardware and software to build innovative, practical working prototypes.

Whether you're passionate about IoT, AI, Embedded Systems, Robotics, Full Stack, Cloud, Computer Vision, Smart Automation, Web3, or Agentic Commerce, FusioniX is your platform to build and innovate.

Please use this Template: [Download](https://www.canva.com/design/DAHSKhhyp4Y/wcuf7vO6wiiPgsLOQtCqPw/edit)
**🏆Prize Pool: ₹30,000+**

Win exciting prizes worth up to ₹50,000.

Along with prizes, participants get certificates, recognition, goodies & swags, networking opportunities with mentors and industry experts, and a chance to showcase their solutions.



**Team Size**

3–4 members per team

Registration is free.
Inter-college teams are allowed.




**Event**

Duration: 24 Hours
Round 1: Online
Final Hackathon (Rounds 2 & 3): Offline at UEM Kolkata


**Eligibility**

Open to students pursuing:

B.Tech / B.E.
M.Tech / M.E.
Engineering or Technology programs from recognized institutions

Students from any engineering specialization can participate.



**Tracks**
Sub Track 1 — x402-Powered Applications

Build applications powered by x402, exploring programmable payments, automated transactions, and digital commerce.

Sub Track 2 — Agentic Commerce Infrastructure

Build infrastructure enabling AI agents to discover, negotiate, transact, and operate autonomously in digital commerce.

Sub Track 3 — Developer Tooling & Frameworks

Create developer tools, SDKs, libraries, frameworks, APIs, or platforms that improve the software development experience.

Sub Track 4 — Biotech

Build technology-driven solutions at the intersection of biology and innovation. Explore AI, computational biology, bioinformatics, healthcare, agriculture, lab automation, and other applications that use technology to address real-world challenges in life sciences .

Sub Track 5 —  AI for Real-World Impact

Build innovative AI-powered solutions that address meaningful real-world problems. From education and sustainability to accessibility, finance, agriculture, cybersecurity, and smart communities, use AI to create practical solutions with measurable impact.

Sub Track 6 — Open Source

Build impactful open-source solutions that encourage collaboration, transparency, and community-driven development. Create tools, platforms, libraries, or applications that others can use, extend, and contribute to.


**Competition Format**
Round 1 — Concept Qualifier (Online)

Submit a minimum 5-slide Pitch Deck (PPT/PDF) covering:
PPt format: https://canva.link/uhjmqki7duf082q
Team Introduction
Problem Analysis
Proposed Solution
Hardware & Software Architecture
Technology Stack

Evaluation: Problem Understanding, Technical Feasibility, Innovation, and Clarity of Presentation.

⚠️ **Important**: The Round 1 idea is only for evaluation. Qualified teams will receive entirely new problem statements during the offline hackathon.

**Round 2 — Hybrid Build & Final Offline Round**

Teams will work on their complete solution by assembling hardware, developing software, designing the system architecture, integrating components, testing, debugging, and preparing a working prototype.

As this is a hybrid competition, teams may use hardware, software, or a combination of both according to their project requirements.

Participants should bring their own hardware whenever possible. Limited hardware support may be available.

Teams must complete and demonstrate their working solution during this round and submit the final source code, documentation, and required project deliverables before the deadline.

**🤖 AI Usage Policy**

AI tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Claude may be used for learning, brainstorming, debugging, documentation, and productivity.

However:

AI must not replace genuine problem-solving.
Blind copy-pasting without understanding is prohibited.
Primarily AI-generated or plagiarized projects will be disqualified.
Judges may ask technical questions to verify understanding.

Innovation and originality matter.


**📜 General Rules**
Major development must be done during the hackathon.
Teams must work independently.
Pre-built complete solutions are not allowed.
Bring your own laptops and hardware whenever possible.
Internet, workspace, power supply, meals, and accommodation (where applicable) will be provided.
Organizers may modify schedules if required.
Plagiarism or unfair means may lead to disqualification.
Judges' decisions will be final.


**🏅 Judging Criteria**

Projects will be evaluated on:

Innovation & Creativity • Technical Implementation • Functionality • Hardware–Software Integration • Market Potential • Scalability • Presentation & Demonstration • Teamwork


**🎁 What Participants Receive**
Participation Certificate
Prizes & Recognition
Goodies & Swags
Networking with mentors and industry experts
Opportunity to showcase innovative engineering solutions

name: BOSS Battle
tagline: Enter the arena. Ship the code. Become the BOSS.
desc:
## About BOSS Battle

Bitshala builds and teaches Bitcoin Open Source Software — that's the "BOSS" in our name, and also the joke behind this one. Between cohort-based learning on Bitcoin's protocol and privacy stack, and the invite-only BOSS Summit that gathers India's sharpest Bitcoin OSS builders twice a year, we've mostly kept things small and deep. BOSS Battle flips that: it's virtual, it's open, and it's a hackathon instead of a summit.

Three boss fights this round:

- **Privacy** — build tools that make Bitcoin harder to surveil and easier to use without leaking who you are.
- **Nostr** — build on the protocol rewriting what censorship-resistant identity and communication look like.
- **AI** — bring AI into the Bitcoin/Nostr stack: agents, tooling, automation — whatever pushes it forward.

You don't need a GitHub history full of BIPs to show up. Beginners get workshops, mentors, and a community that answers questions instead of gatekeeping them. Experienced builders get a chance to finally prototype the thing they've been meaning to build, surrounded by people who actually get it.

No stage, no suits — just your terminal and three boss fights between you and the leaderboard.

**Ship code. Beat the boss.**

tagline: With great power comes great responsibility!
desc:
# HackVerse: Into the Web

**HackVerse: Into the Web** is a **SpiderMan-themed, story-driven hackathon** organized by the **IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (IEEE RAS), VIT Chennai Student Chapter**, as part of **TechnoVIT 2026**.

Unlike a conventional hackathon, HackVerse is designed as a **24-hour journey through three progressively challenging sprints**, taking participants from rapid ideation to competitive problem-solving and finally to building a real-world, deploy-ready product.

> **With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility!**

*Exclusive Prizes for Hardware Track*

***Win SpiderMan Masks and Goodies for best innovation!***

## Into the Web:

### 🕸️ 1. Web-Slinger Sprint [Rapid Vibe Coding]:

Kick things off with a high-energy **rapid vibe-coding challenge**.

Teams get limited time to turn an idea into a functional prototype using modern frameworks, AI coding tools, APIs, and whatever technology they choose.

**Focus:** Ideation • Rapid Prototyping • AI-Assisted Development • Creativity

### 🕷️ 2. Spider-Sense Sprint [Competitive Coding]:

Next, put your problem-solving skills to the test.

Teams face a **mini competitive-coding challenge** involving algorithms, logic, and DSA. Speed and accuracy matter as you compete against other builders.

**Focus:** DSA • Algorithms • Logic • Speed • Problem Solving

### 🌐 3. Multiverse Sprint [Build for the Real World]:

Now comes the main challenge.

Teams take their ideas beyond prototypes and build a **functional, deployment-ready product** with real-world applicability, meaningful technical implementation, and a strong user experience.

Build **anything, in any domain** - AI, robotics and IoT, fintech, cybersecurity, , automation, Web3 etc.

**Focus:** Product Engineering • Deployment • Scalability • Real-World Impact

## 🚀 Open Innovation

**No fixed problem statement. No fixed domain. No fixed technology stack.**

Have an idea worth building? Build it.

Whether you're creating an AI agent, robotics system, fintech platform, healthcare solution, automation tool, or something nobody has thought of yet, HackVerse gives you the freedom to build what you believe in.

## 👥 Team Up

Teams consist of **3–5 members**.


## 🕸️ The Story

HackVerse isn't just a sequence of rounds. It's a **hero's journey**.

You start as a builder entering the Web. Each sprint introduces a new challenge, pushing your team to think faster, solve harder problems, and build better.

**Web-Slinger → Spider-Sense → Multiverse**

By the end of the 24 hours, your mission is simple:

**Take an idea. Build it. Deploy it. Prove it.**

## ⚡ The Mission

HackVerse is built for people who don't want to just **attend** a hackathon.

It's for people who want to **build under pressure, compete, experiment, collaborate, and ship something real**.

**With great power comes great responsibility.**

**Welcome to HackVerse: Into the Web.**

name: What the Hack!
desc:
​A hackathon for engineers who want to spend a day building things that absolutely did not need to exist.

​No problem statements. No pitch decks. No startup ideas. Just a simple challenge: build something deliberately useless, absurd, or spectacularly counterproductive and make it technically impressive.

# ​The Idea
​What The Hack is the next edition of Hack for Nothing, bringing back the same rule: there is no problem to solve.

​The only valid reason to build something is:

> ​“Technically, this is possible.”


# ​What Counts?
​The bar is simple: genuinely useless or actively counterproductive.

​Build software that solves a problem nobody has. Make an easy task dramatically harder. Build absurd hardware. Create a robot that undoes its own work. Spend six hours engineering an elaborate solution to a joke that could have been solved in five minutes.

​The more technically impressive the solution, the more questionable the decision to build it should be.

**​Practical utility is a disqualifier.**

If a judge can imagine a real user, you may have accidentally built something useful.

# ​Do’s
- ​Build something you’d be slightly embarrassed to explain to your parents.
- ​Over-engineer freely.
- ​Commit completely to the bit.
- Spend an unreasonable amount of time solving an unreasonable problem.

# ​Don’ts

- ​Don’t sneak a real use case into your demo halfway through.
- Don’t turn a startup idea into a joke just to qualify.
- Don’t violate consent or privacy.
- Don’t show up with something pre-built.

# ​The Only Question
​Can you build it? You probably shouldn’t.

**​Build it anyway.**

desc:

DoraHacks 2.0 is a global, fully remote a global hackathon designed to help participants transform their ideas into real-world products using AI and no-code technologies.

Unlike traditional hackathons that primarily focus on building prototypes, DoraHacks follows a **two-phase execution model**:

### **Phase 1: Build — Turning Ideas Into Products**

Participants collaborate in teams to build functional MVPs using any tools, frameworks, or platforms of their choice.

The focus is not only on creating something technically impressive but on solving meaningful problems and building products that can create real user value.

### **Phase 2: Launch — Taking Products To The Market**

The second phase focuses on helping teams move beyond development and successfully launch their products.

### Participants will receive guidance on:

- Product positioning
- Launch strategy
- Storytelling
- Community building
- User acquisition
- Product Hunt & Peerlist launches
- Collecting early user feedback

The goal is simple:

**Every team should leave not only with a product, but with their first users, market validation, and a launch story.**

---
---

## Finding Your Teammates

#### Option 1: Build With GWY Community

You can form teams with other fellows. Use the community to find:

- Someone who complements your skills
- Someone who shares your ambition
- Someone who is ready to show up for 72 hours

#### Option 2: Bring Your Own Team

You can also participate with:

- Friends
- College teammates
- Existing collaborators
- Professional networks

---
---

# Mentor Ecosystem

To ensure participants receive support across every stage of the journey, DoraHacks 2.0 brings together a network of **60+ mentors** from diverse backgrounds including:

- AI & Technology
- Product Management
- Startup Growth
- Marketing & Distribution
- Design & User Experience
- Content & Storytelling
- Community Building

Mentors will support teams through:

- Product feedback sessions
- Technical guidance
- Launch strategy
- Growth experiments
- Final pitch preparation

---
---

# Product Launch Requirements

To ensure every project moves beyond a prototype, participating teams will follow these guidelines:

- | Product Ownership | Each product must have a standalone account or be launched through the team members' existing accounts.
- | Building Tools | Teams are free to use any AI tools, no-code platforms, frameworks, or technologies.
- | Product Launch | Every product must be launched on Product Hunt.
- | User Validation | Teams must onboard a minimum of 50 users and collect feedback
- | Feedback Collection | Teams are encouraged to collect public reviews and testimonials 
- | Content Journey | Teams must create minimum 4 content pieces documenting their journey

# Beyond Hack Hours

DoraHacks 2.0 does not end with submission.
The strongest teams will continue receiving support through:

- Community visibility
- Product feedback
- Founder connections
- Growth opportunities
- Future DoraDAO ecosystem opportunities

The objective is to create products that continue growing even after the hackathon concludes.

# Expected Outcomes

By the end of DoraHacks 2.0, participants will have:

✅ Built a functional AI/no-code product
✅ Launched publicly on Product Hunt
✅ Acquired their first 50+ users
✅ Learned product distribution & growth
✅ Built with guidance from 60+ industry mentors
✅ Created a public portfolio of their entrepreneurial journey

name: Agentic Commerce Hackathon
tagline: Build agents that act, shop, book, renew and pay.
desc:
> **48 hours. Online. $70,000 in cash + credits.**

**Most AI products stop after giving an answer. We want to see what happens when the agent can finish the job.**

Over 48 hours, build a working product where an AI agent can discover, decide and complete a transaction using Prava. 

**It could shop across merchants, book a trip, manage a subscription, procure software, reserve a table or create a new kind of commerce experience.**

We want useful products that can live beyond the hackathon - not slide decks or demos built only for judging.

## What is Prava?

Prava is the payments and trust layer for AI agents. With Prava you can enable your AI agents to make purchase on any merchant online. 

Prava gives AI agents a one-time card/wallet with limits set by the user. You can integrate Prava using API/SDK or MCP & CLI. 

- **Prava [Docs](https://docs.prava.space/)**
- **Prava [Developer Dashboard](https://dashboard.prava.space/) (SDK/API)**

## Who should apply?

Apply if there is an idea you keep coming back to and want to put in people's hands.

You could be a **student, developer, designer, operator, researcher or founder.** You may already be building, or you may only have an idea and want 48 focused hours to learn whether it works. **What matters is that you want to build something real and take the idea seriously.**

**Already working on a product?** 
You are welcome to apply. During the hackathon, you must ship a clearly new workflow or use case powered by Prava. Existing work can be the starting point; it cannot be the entire submission.

## How participation works?

1. Apply through Devfolio.
2. We review applications on a rolling basis.
3. If accepted, RSVP within 3 days.
4. Build solo or form a team of up to 4 accepted participants.
5. Join [Discord](https://discord.gg/D2589RGK6) for announcements, support and team formation.

**Every team member must apply and be accepted.**
Discord is required. If you need teammates, use the team-formation channels there.

## What you need to build?

Your submission must include meaningful work completed during the hackathon, **use Prava as a real part of the product, and demonstrate an agent completing or enabling a transaction**. 

Show a working flow, explain the user and problem, and disclose anything that existed before the event.

## Awards and credits

Projects will be considered for the overall competition and every award for which they qualify. More details in Prizes section.

Every approved participant gets $100 in credits from OpenAI. Winner credits are listed separately. 

## What we will judge?

We will look at whether the product works, solves a clear problem, uses an agent to take meaningful action, handles payments clearly and could become a real product.

Individual awards may emphasize startup potential, consumer experience, B2B value, OpenAI usage, and Prava integration. 

## Discord, office hours and build requests

Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/D2589RGK6) with the link below.

Office hours will be held one week before the hackathon. 

**If you're out of ideas, check our [RFH:  Requests for Hacks library](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qCyXHa8M6p_dDLzwB39D_jpRHUgVXdQ6/view?usp=sharing).** 

Already building something relevant to this hackathon? Post what you are working on, tag **@PravaPayments** on X and the team may fast-track strong applications.

More partners, mentors and judges will be announced soon.

name: Port Mortem 2026 - Code Resurrection Hackathon
tagline: Port the Code. Prove the Performance.
desc:
# All that you need to know about Port Mortem 2026 | Code Resurrection Hackathon

## About the Hackathon:

Port Mortem 2026 is a 72-hour online hackathon focused on AI-assisted software migration and cross-language code porting. Participants will rewrite a real open-source project from one programming language to another while preserving its functionality, correctness, and engineering quality.

Rather than simply generating code, teams are expected to demonstrate behavioral equivalence through testing, benchmarking, and documentation. The challenge emphasizes engineering discipline, software quality, and production-ready implementations.

**Event website:** https://coderesurrection.com/2026

**Stay Updated:** Join the official Hackathon Raptors Discord server for all announcements, rule clarifications, repository releases, submission instructions, FAQs, and live event support. Important updates will be communicated exclusively through Discord. You can find the Discord invite on our website: https://raptors.dev.

---

## Eligibility:

* Open to students, professionals, researchers, and software developers worldwide.
* Participants from any college, university, organization, or country are welcome.
* Solo participation is allowed.
* Teams may consist of 1–4 members.
* Inter-college teams are allowed.
* Inter-specialization and cross-disciplinary teams are allowed.

---

## Event Format:

### Registration Phase:

* Register individually or as a team.
* Join the official Discord server for announcements, discussions, and support.

### Repository Selection:

At hackathon kickoff, participants will choose a repository from a curated pool of eligible open-source projects or submit an alternative repository for approval (subject to organizer guidelines).

### Development Phase (72 Hours):

Teams will:

* Port the selected project into the target programming language.
* Preserve the original behavior and functionality.
* Validate correctness using the original test suite whenever possible.
* Benchmark the implementation.
* Document architectural decisions and implementation trade-offs.

### Submission:

Each team must submit:

* Public GitHub repository
* Build instructions
* Working implementation
* Benchmark report
* DECISIONS.md
* Differential testing/fuzzing artifacts (if applicable)
* Demo video

---

## Tracks:

Participants may choose one of the following migration tracks:

* C → Rust
* Zig → Rust
* TypeScript → Go
* Python → Rust
* Go → Rust
* JavaScript → Go or Rust
* C → Zig
* Open Pair (Any Language → Any Language)

---

## Judging Criteria:

Projects will be evaluated on:

### Functionality & Reliability (40%)

Build quality, successful execution, and test suite compatibility.

### Behavioral Equivalence (30%)

Accuracy of the migration, differential testing, benchmarking, and performance analysis.

### Code Quality (20%)

Idiomatic implementation, maintainability, engineering practices, and documentation.

### Innovation (10%)

Creative solutions, architectural improvements, and valuable enhancements.

Bonus points may be awarded for:

* Differential fuzzing
* Minimal unsafe code
* Discovering bugs in the original project
* Exceptional engineering documentation

---

## Rules:

* Team size: 1–4 members.
* All development must be completed during the official 72-hour hackathon period.
* AI coding assistants and developer tools are permitted.
* The submitted repository must be public at submission time.
* The project must build using a single documented command.
* Source-language runtime wrappers or proxy implementations are not permitted.
* Teams should preserve the original test suite wherever feasible. Any modifications must be documented.
* Participants must comply with all open-source licensing requirements.
* Plagiarism or submission of pre-existing ports may result in disqualification.

---

## Timeline:

* **Registration Opens:** 29 June 2026
* **Hackathon Begins:** 31 July 2026
* **Submission Deadline:** 3 August 2026
* **Judging:** 3–13 August 2026
* **Winner Announcement:** 14 August 2026

desc:
# HackGenome 2026

## Where Student Ideas Become Real Innovations

⚠️ **IMPORTANT:** HackGenome 2026 is exclusively open to currently enrolled students of **KIET Deemed to be University**. Applications from students of other institutions or pass-outs will not be considered.

HackGenome 2026 is an online AI hackathon organized by the **Department of CSIT, KIET Deemed to be University** in collaboration with **Rabbitt AI**.

The hackathon aims to bring together students who are passionate about innovation, technology, and problem-solving. Participants will have the opportunity to develop impactful AI-driven solutions, transform ideas into working products, and present their vision before an expert panel.

Whether you're interested in Artificial Intelligence, Software Development, Design, Cybersecurity, Automation, Education Technology, Healthcare Innovation, or any other technology-driven domain, HackGenome provides a platform to build solutions that can create meaningful impact.

---

## Why Participate?

* Work on real-world problems
* Build innovative AI-powered solutions
* Showcase your creativity and technical skills
* Gain hands-on project-building experience
* Receive certificates of participation
* Compete for exciting rewards and recognition
* Network with mentors and industry experts

---

## Special Opportunity

🏆 **Winning team(s) will receive an opportunity to present and participate in a Hackathon at IIT Delhi in July 2026.**

---

## Important Dates

📅 Registration Deadline: **8 June 2026**

📄 PPT Submission Deadline: **12 June 2026, 11:59 pm**

🎤 Final Round Presentations: **14 June 2026 (Online)**

---

## Eligibility

This hackathon is exclusively open to students of **KIET Deemed to be University**.

---

## Team Size

* Minimum Team Size: **2 Members**
* Maximum Team Size: **4 Members**

Participants may form interdisciplinary teams with members from different domains and academic backgrounds.

---

# Problem Statements

Participants may choose **any one** of the following tracks.

---

## 🚀 Track 1: Talking Rabbitt – AI-Powered Business Intelligence Dashboard

### Domain

Business Intelligence | Enterprise AI | Analytics

### Challenge

Build an AI-powered conversational dashboard capable of:

* Analyzing Excel/CSV datasets
* Detecting trends and anomalies
* Generating dashboards automatically
* Answering business questions using natural language
* Providing recommendations and forecasts

### Expected Features

* Conversational AI Assistant
* Dynamic KPI Dashboard
* Trend & Anomaly Detection
* Forecasting Engine
* Recommendation System
* Voice/Text Interaction

---

## 🎨 Track 2: AI-Powered Personal Brand Marketing Engine

### Domain

Creator Economy | AI Marketing | Personal Branding

### Challenge

Build an AI platform that helps users grow their personal brand by:

* Analyzing profile and audience behavior
* Generating content automatically
* Scheduling posts intelligently
* Optimizing engagement across platforms

### Expected Features

* AI Content Generation
* LinkedIn/Instagram/X Integrations
* Content Calendar Intelligence
* Automated Scheduling
* Audience Analytics
* Multi-platform Optimization

---

## 📈 Track 3: AI Competitor Strategy Analyzer

### Domain

Marketing Intelligence | D2C | Business Strategy

### Challenge

Build an AI-powered competitor intelligence platform that can:

* Monitor competitors
* Analyze campaigns and content strategies
* Detect emerging trends
* Recommend strategic actions

### Expected Features

* Competitor Tracking Dashboard
* Campaign Analysis Engine
* Strategy Recommendation System
* Trend Prediction
* Market Intelligence Assistant

---

## 🔍 Track 4: Signals Harvesting Engine – Agentic AI Workflow System

### Domain

Lead Intelligence | AI Automation | Sales Intelligence

### Challenge

Build an AI-powered system that automatically captures business signals, identifies opportunities, prioritizes leads, and triggers intelligent workflows.

### Expected Features

* Signal Monitoring Engine
* Intent Analysis
* Lead Scoring System
* Automated Workflows
* CRM Integration
* Opportunity Intelligence Dashboard

---

## 👨‍💼 Track 5: Agentic AI HRMS & Hiring Automation Platform

### Domain

HRTech | Enterprise Automation | AI Agents

### Challenge

Build a complete AI-powered HR ecosystem capable of automating:

* Resume Screening
* Candidate Evaluation
* AI Interviews
* Employee Onboarding
* Payroll Processing
* Leave Management
* Employee Support

### Expected Features

* Resume Parsing Engine
* AI Candidate Ranking
* AI Interview Assistant
* Payroll Automation
* Leave & Attendance Management
* Conversational HR Assistant
* Workforce Analytics Dashboard

---

# Judging Criteria

| Criteria                          | Weightage |
| --------------------------------- | --------- |
| Innovation & Idea Clarity         | 20%       |
| Technical Implementation          | 25%       |
| AI & Agentic Workflow Integration | 20%       |
| UI/UX & Product Design            | 15%       |
| Scalability & Business Potential  | 10%       |
| Presentation & Communication      | 10%       |

---

## Submission Requirements

Each team must submit:

* Working Prototype / Functional Demo
* Project Documentation
* AI Workflow & System Architecture
* Pitch Deck (10–12 Slides)
* Final Presentation

---

## Community & Updates

Join our official WhatsApp Community to receive announcements, submission updates, and important notices:

https://forms.gle/WAWAWsLfPuJoT61y9

---

## Platform

All registrations and submissions will be managed through **Devfolio**.

---

## Contact

For any queries regarding HackGenome 2026, please contact:

📧 [hackgenome@hotmail.com](mailto:hackgenome@hotmail.com)

---

### Build. Innovate. Impact.

### Welcome to HackGenome 2026.

# 🚀 Algorand Builders Berlin: Agentic Commerce x402 Hackathon

​📅 June 6th 9:00 am – June 7th 21:00 pm
📍 42 Berlin, Harzer Strasse 42, 12059 Berlin
🏠 On-site event (at least one team member must be present on-site to pitch)

# ​🌐 Build the Future of Internet-Native Payments

​Join us for a 36-hour hackathon exploring x402 payments — an open payment protocol for internet-native payments built for the age of AI and autonomous agents.

​This event is designed to help you build real solutions to real-world problems.

​We’re especially interested in projects applying x402 to areas such as: agentic commerce, paid APIs, data access, DeFi tooling, RWA services, and tokenization workflows.

**​Most importantly, we’re looking for teams committed to continuing beyond the hackathon.
**
# ​👤 Who should join?
Experienced developers
​First-time hackers
​Entrepreneurs
​Designers
​Curious builders

​Anyone who wants to vibe-code the next big thing in payments

# ​🧩 Two-Tier System: New & Existing Projects

​We’re building a diverse ecosystem and supporting builders at all stages:

​**New Projects**: Start fresh during the hackathon (no pre-built code)
**Existing Projects**: Already building? Integrate x402, add Algorand, or extend your product (Web2 or Web3)

​We welcome everyone.

**​We’ll provide**:
​🛠️ Workshops and technical guidance
​🤝 Mentorship
​🤖 AI tools to accelerate development
​⚡ A collaborative, high-energy builder environment
​🤝 Team matching and networking

​Already have a team? Great.
Have an idea but no team? Perfect.
Have neither? Even better.

**​Join the community** to find teammates, share ideas, and stay updated: ​Use the **[Telegram group](https://t.me/+GUyxFWJbL582ZjAy)** for team building, networking, and hackathon updates.
We’ll actively help match people with complementary skills.

# ​📜 Rules & Requirements

​👥** Team size**: 1–5 participants

​🌍 **Remote participation**: Allowed, but at least one team member must be on-site and present the final pitch

​🤖 **AI usage**: Fully allowed and encouraged — we will provide Algorand AI tooling and templates

​Submissions will be judged on criteria such as technical sophistication, creativity, usability, value proposition, and potential ecosystem impact. While these criteria guide evaluation, all final decisions regarding winners and prize allocations remain at the Algorand Foundation’s sole discretion.

name: Devlynix Buildathon 1.0
tagline: Escape Tutorial Hell. Build Real Solutions.
desc:
Welcome to Devlynix Buildathon 1.0, an asynchronous, weekend-long mini-hackathon designed specifically to help you transition from watching tutorials to building practical, real-world projects.

This hackathon focuses on the "Idea-to-MVP Sprint" model. We aren't looking for perfect code; we are looking for strong problem-solving, clean design, and a solid technical approach.

# **⚠️ IMPORTANT: MANDATORY STEP**

All official announcements, squad formations, and shortlisting results will be shared EXCLUSIVELY on our WhatsApp handles. Joining both is mandatory for participation.

👉 Join our WhatsApp Channel: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VbCzGzaJpe8chzjL0w1F
👉 Join our Community Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EJrdn43jObx00BKnp444Rj

# ​📅 **Event Overview**

**Format:** 48-Hour Asynchronous Online Hackathon
**Team Size**: 1 to 4 Members per Squad
**Goal:** Build a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) addressing specific community tech challenges.

# 🛠️ The Challenge: Choose Your Problem Statement
Squads must select one of the following real-world challenges to solve. Your goal is to build a functional MVP with a clean User Interface.

> **1. The Developer Proof-of-Work Platform 🚀**
Many developers build great projects but lose them in scattered GitHub repositories. Build a centralized showcase directory where developers can host their deployed projects, tag their tech stack, and attach demo videos. Include filtering options (e.g., MERN, Web3, AI) for easy discovery.

>**2. The "Execution-First" Accountability Tracker 🔥**
Students often get stuck in "tutorial hell." Build a web dashboard that tracks a user's daily or weekly "build streak" based on actual project execution. The app should prompt users with "What did you code today?", visualize their consistency, and reward them with milestones.

>**3. The Skill-Based Teammate Matchmaker 🤝**
Finding the right teammates for hackathons or side projects is a major hurdle. Design a user-directory system where individuals can create profiles highlighting their specific skills (e.g., UI/UX, React, AI) and proficiency levels. Implement a search and filter mechanism to connect users.

> **4. The Crowdsourced Learning Vault 📚**
The internet is flooded with scattered resources. Build an organized, community-driven resource hub where users can submit and categorize high-quality links, tools, and guides. Include an upvote/downvote system so the best resources naturally rise to the top.

>**5. The Micro-Event & Submission Portal 🎯**
Small tech communities struggle to manage asynchronous events through chaotic group chats. Create a streamlined event dashboard displaying hackathon details, rules, and deadlines. It must feature a dedicated submission portal where teams can upload their final deliverables.

# 🎯 What You Need to Submit (The Deliverables)
To successfully complete the hackathon, your squad must submit the following three items:

 > **1. The Website MVP (Minimum Viable Product)**

**Build What You Can:** If you are a beginner, building just a clean, functional frontend MVP is completely fine. If you have the skills, you are highly encouraged to build the full-stack version (Frontend + Backend/Database)!

> **2. The Pitch Video (Max 10 Minutes)**

This is your final presentation! Record your screen and your voice.
**How to do it:** Walk us through your PPT first, and then give a live demo of your Website MVP.
**The Vibe:** Be confident! Explain your thought process, why you designed the UI a certain way, and how the code logic works.

# 📅 Buildathon 1.0: Official Timeline
**Phase 1: Registration & Concept Submission**
Date: 4th May
Duration: 24 Hours
Task: Register your team on Devfolio and start working on any problem statement given above.

**Phase 2: The 48-Hour Build Sprint**
Task: Start coding your MVP (Minimum Viable Product). This is the main development phase where you build your frontend/full-stack solution.
Submission: Keep your Deployed Website Link.

**Phase 3: Final Submission & Video Pitch**
Final Deliverables: 
1. Deployed Website Link. (In Project Links)
2. GitHub Repo URL. (In Project Links)
3. Final Video Demo (Max 10 Minutes):(YouTube link)

Important: The Devfolio submission portal will automatically close at 11:59 PM on 6th May.

**📅 Important Instructions for Participants:**

Strict Deadlines: Submissions after the round deadline will lead to automatic disqualification.

Communication: All shortlisting announcements will be made via the official Devlynix WhatsApp group and Devfolio notifications.

# 📊 Evaluation Criteria
Judges will evaluate your submissions out of 100 Points based on these 4 pillars:

**Problem-Solution Fit (25 Points):** How practical and realistic is your solution?
**UI/UX & Design (25 Points):** Is the layout user-friendly, clean, and adhering to the 'Silent Coder' aesthetic?
**Technical Logic (25 Points):** How functional is the code, or how clearly is the technical architecture defined?
**The Final Pitch (25 Points):** How well was the product explained and demonstrated in the video?

*Get ready to build. Good luck, Squads! Let's build something awesome. 🛠️🔥*

Welcome to **Cepheus 2.0 2026**, a **24-hour Hackathon** where **innovation, creativity, and collaboration** take center stage!  
This hackathon is a **beacon for developers, designers, and problem-solvers** looking to push the boundaries of technology and create groundbreaking solutions.

## 💡 Why Join Cepheus Hackathon?  
✅ **Code & Innovate** – Tackle real-world challenges with cutting-edge tech.

✨ Get ready to **code, innovate, and make an impact**! 🌟  

---

## 🏆 Rewards & Recognition

### 💰 **₹50,000 Prize Pool — Compete. Build. Win Big.**

This isn't just another hackathon; it’s your chance to claim a share of the **₹50,000 bounty**. Whether you're a seasoned builder or a rising star, the stakes are high and the rewards are waiting.

---

### **The Podium**

🥇 **Grand Winner**
**₹25,000** + Certificate of Excellence

🥈 **1st Runner-Up**
**₹15,000** + Certificate of Excellence

🥉 **2nd Runner-Up**
**₹10,000** + Certificate of Excellence

---


*Note: Additional special category prizes and sponsor bounties may be announced closer to the event. Stay tuned for updates!*

---

## 🧩 Problem Statements (Themes)

Choose from one of our impactful problem statements and build a solution that matters!

### 1️⃣ Digital Asset Protection: Protecting the Integrity of Digital Sports Media
**The Challenge:** Sports organizations generate massive volumes of high-value digital media that rapidly scatter across global platforms, making it nearly impossible to track. This vast visibility gap leaves proprietary content highly vulnerable to widespread digital misappropriation, unauthorized redistribution, and intellectual property violations.  
**🎯 Objective:** Develop a scalable, innovative solution to identify, track, and flag unauthorized use or misappropriation of official sports media across the internet. Enable organizations to proactively authenticate their digital assets and detect anomalies in content propagation in near real-time.

### 2️⃣ Rapid Crisis Response: Accelerated Emergency Response and Crisis Coordination in Hospitality
**The Challenge:** Hospitality venues face unpredictable, high-stakes emergencies that demand instantaneous, coordinated reactions to protect lives and property. During a crisis, critical information is often siloed, fracturing communication between distressed guests, on-site staff, and first responders.  
**🎯 Objective:** Design a robust solution to instantly detect, report, and synchronize crisis response efforts across a decentralized hospitality ecosystem. Eliminate fragmented communication by creating a highly reliable bridge between distressed individuals, active personnel, and emergency services.

### 3️⃣ Smart Supply Chains: Resilient Logistics and Dynamic Supply Chain Optimization
**The Challenge:** Modern global supply chains manage millions of concurrent shipments across highly complex and inherently volatile transportation networks. Critical transit disruptions ranging from sudden weather events to hidden operational bottlenecks are chronically identified only after delivery timelines are already compromised.  
**🎯 Objective:** Design a scalable system capable of continuously analyzing multifaceted transit data to preemptively detect and flag potential supply chain disruptions. Formulate dynamic mechanisms that instantly execute or recommend highly optimized route adjustments before localized bottlenecks cascade into broader delays.

### 4️⃣ Unbiased AI Decision: Ensuring Fairness and Detecting Bias in Automated Decisions
**The Challenge:** Computer programs now make life-changing decisions about who gets a job, a bank loan, or even medical care. However, if these programs learn from flawed or unfair historical data, they will repeat and amplify those exact same discriminatory mistakes.  
**🎯 Objective:** Build a clear, accessible solution to thoroughly inspect data sets and software models for hidden unfairness or discrimination. Provide organizations with an easy way to measure, flag, and fix harmful bias before their systems impact real people.

### 5️⃣ Smart Resource Allocation: Data-Driven Volunteer Coordination for Social Impact
**The Challenge:** Local social groups and NGOs collect a lot of important information about community needs through paper surveys and field reports. However, this valuable data is often scattered across different places, making it hard to see the biggest problems clearly.  
**🎯 Objective:** Design a powerful system that gathers scattered community information to clearly show the most urgent local needs. Build a smart way to quickly match and connect available volunteers with the specific tasks and areas where they are needed most.

### 6️⃣ Web3 & Decentralized Future: Building Trust in a Trustless World
**The Challenge:** Despite the promise of decentralization, Web3 adoption remains hindered by poor user experience, lack of transparency, and limited real-world utility. Everyday users struggle to interact with blockchain ecosystems due to complexity, security risks such as smart contract vulnerabilities and wallet fraud, and the absence of accessible tools that bridge Web2 habits with Web3 infrastructure.  
**🎯 Objective:** Build a practical, user-centric Web3 application that solves a real-world problem using blockchain, smart contracts, decentralized identity, DAOs, DeFi, or token-based incentive systems. Your solution should prioritize accessibility, security, and genuine utility — demonstrating that decentralized technology can be both powerful and approachable for mainstream users.

**BitBox 6.0** is the flagship annual technology event organized by the Google Developer Groups (GDG) chapter at Jaypee Institute of Information Technology (JIIT), Sector 128, Noida. KINDLY CONTACT AT HACKIT.BVCOEND.AC.IN FOR QUESTIONS.**
Hosted by the **Department of Information Technology** at **Bharati Vidyapeeth’s College of Engineering (BVCOE), New Delhi**, **Hack.IT@BVP 3.0** is a premier technical symposium designed for passionate innovators. This iteration brings together diverse disciplines to architect solutions centered on **digital trust, data accountability**, and the strategic pillars of the **G20 priorities**.

---

### **The Experience**
Designed as a rigorous **two-day hybrid event**, the program is structured to take participants from initial conceptualization to a finished technical product:

* **Phase I: Ideathon** 💡- 11 April 2026
    A forum for high-level brainstorming and strategic pitching, where teams present impactful ideas that address contemporary global challenges.
* **Phase II: Hackathon** 💻-
Online rounds on 16 April 2026
 Grand Finale on 18 April 2026
    A transition into rapid development, where participants build and refine functional prototypes under time-sensitive conditions.


All teams chosen to present their ideas in the ideathon are automatically selected for the first round of the Hackathon.
The presentation round for the Ideathon will be on 11 April 2026 on the BVCOE Campus.
The first and second round of the Hackathon will be online on 16th April whereas the final round will be on held on the BVCOE Campus on 18 April 2026.

Please mail at hackit@bvcoend.ac.in for any further doubts.
---

### **Technical Domains & Innovation**
**Hack.IT@BVP 3.0** emphasizes the intersection of advanced technology and ethical design. Participants are encouraged to explore:

* **Emerging Technologies:** Utilizing **Artificial Intelligence**, **Cybersecurity** frameworks, and **Blockchain** to solve complex problems.
* **Regulatory Alignment:** Designing systems that are not only technologically superior but also **legally compliant** and architecturally sound.
* **Social Responsibility:** Creating data-driven solutions that prioritize user accountability and global digital safety.

---

### **Mentorship and Growth**
This event serves as an incubator for professional development, providing participants with:

* **Expert Guidance:** Direct access to **industry veterans** and **distinguished academicians** for technical and strategic mentorship.
* **Collaborative Environment:** An opportunity to network with a peer group of engineers and technologists from across the country.
* **Tangible Impact:** A platform to showcase innovations that have the potential to influence real-world digital policy and infrastructure.

---
Please note: As this is not a 24 hour offline hackathin, no accomodation will be provided to the participants.
> **Build. Innovate. Impact.**
> Join us at **Hack.IT@BVP 3.0** to transform your vision into the next standard of digital excellence.
Dive into digital trust and data accountability — here are some idea tracks to get you started, but we welcome all ideas!
Some exampls tracks for the hackathon are as follows:
1.Consent-Aware AI Pipelines
•	AI systems increasingly rely on personal datasets without dynamic consent tracking or data lifecycle visibility.
•	How can intelligent systems automatically verify consent validity, enforce data minimisation, and prevent unauthorised data usage in AI model training and inference?
2.Privacy-Preserving Age Verification Intelligence
•	Age detection systems frequently rely on intrusive identity data collection or inaccurate heuristics.
•	How might AI enable accurate yet privacy-preserving age assurance mechanisms using minimal personal data exposure?
3.Tamper-Proof Data Consent Ledgers
Consent records today are stored in centralised databases that are prone to manipulation or inconsistencies.
How can decentralised technologies enable immutable, verifiable consent histories accessible across platforms?
4.Real-Time Data Breach Detection & Response Systems
•	Delayed breach detection increases financial loss and reputational damage.
•	 Develop proactive monitoring solutions that detect anomalous data access patterns and trigger automated containment actions.
5.Automated Regulatory Breach Reporting Frameworks
•	Organisations lack efficient systems to notify authorities and users within mandated timelines.
•	 Create secure reporting pipelines that generate compliant alerts and structured incident disclosures.
6.Sector-Specific Sensitive Data Protection Architectures
•	Healthcare, financial, and education platforms face high-impact risks from unauthorized data exposure.
•	 Design adaptive security frameworks ensuring granular access control and high-assurance data protection.
7.Detecting Over-Collection of Personal Data
•	Digital services frequently collect excessive user information beyond functional requirements.
•	 How can analytical models identify redundant data collection patterns and recommend minimisation strategies?
8.Trust Score Modelling for Digital Platforms
•	Users lack measurable indicators of how responsibly platforms handle their personal data
•	 Develop data-driven trust scoring mechanisms based on transparency, compliance signals, and incident history.
9.Privacy-Aware Smart Device Data Governance
•	Connected devices continuously collect behavioural and environmental data with limited user awareness.
•	 How can automated systems enforce contextual data collection policies in smart environments?
10. Miscellanaous
All ideas are welcome. You may bring any project that aligns with the theme.

InternWare - The Internship Cell of IITM, Janakpuri, is organizing Matrix 3.0 happening on April 06-07, 2026, the ultimate Tech Carnival for emerging talent. Our tech carnival is engineered for execution, where ideas are built, not just pitched.

The Hackathon stands as its core highlight, a 36-hour high-energy coding marathon where innovation never pauses. Participants collaborate, build real-world solutions, and push their creativity and problem-solving skills to the limit in a competitive, mentor-driven environment.

**AI & ML**

**HealthTech**

**Sustainability**

- **Technical Implementation:** The project should function properly and demonstrate strong technical execution. Judges will evaluate the complexity, correctness, and quality of the implementation within the given hackathon timeframe.

prizes.desc: **Description:** Teachers often cannot accurately identify whether students truly understand concepts or are just memorizing answers, leading to weak foundations and poor academic outcomes. **Expected Solution** Develop an AI-driven system that analyzes quizzes, assignments, time spent on questions, and error patterns to generate concept-wise understanding scores and learning insights for teachers and students.

prizes.name: Lego & 3D Construction Kits
prizes.desc: **Description:** Building Lego toys and 3D construction kits requires users to follow static instruction manuals and correctly identify parts. Many learners struggle with spatial understanding and multi-step assembly, leading to errors and frustration. Traditional guides cannot observe progress, adapt to a learner’s pace, or provide real-time correction, which reduces engagement and learning efficiency. **Proposed Solution:** We propose an AI-powered assembly assistant that uses computer vision to recognize parts and map them to a digital 3D model. The system provides step-by-step visual guidance through augmented reality or an on-screen interface, highlights correct placement, and gives instant feedback when mistakes occur. This transforms static instructions into an interactive guided experience that improves accuracy, spatial understanding, and user confidence.

Children often lose interest because the cards do not provide interaction, storytelling, or immersive engagement. There is a need for a smart system that can bring cards to life and transform static learning material into an interactive storytelling experience. **Proposed Solution:** We propose an AI-powered storytelling assistant that activates when a user scans an educational card. For example, scanning a toynik nutrition card featuring fruits or vegetables triggers a short interactive story about their benefits. This turns traditional cards into dynamic learning tools that increase engagement, creativity, and knowledge retention.

name: ECLIPSE
tagline: From Idea to Impact, From Vulnerabilities to Victories
desc:
**ECLIPSE** is a national-level hackathon focused on **IoT and Network Security**, designed exclusively for students to solve real-world cybersecurity challenges.

**Sponserd by   ISEA** (Information Security Education and Awareness), MeitY, Government of India

 



**Theme/Problem Statement: IoT Trust & Drift Analytics**

Build a cyber-security lens for IoT networks: score device trust, detect policy drift, and explain exactly why a device looks risky—using only network telemetry.

Detailed Problem Statement Explaination -- [Problem Statement Explaination](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yhGdHr7y61brK8rmcLuvsrX2F9xp1c62/view?usp=sharing) 

**THIS IS A COMPLETE SOFTWARE BASED HACKATHON**

**Background / Context:**

IoT/IIoT devices (cameras, sensors, gateways, smart controllers) are everywhere—and they often can’t run heavy security agents. That makes the network the best place to observe behaviour. In real cyber incidents, compromised or misconfigured devices rarely “announce” themselves; instead, they gradually change how they communicate: new destinations, unusual timing patterns, unexpected protocols, abnormal spikes, or slow drift away from what was previously normal.

Security teams need a system that can answer three things clearly:

Is this device still trustworthy right now?
Is it still behaving within expected “allowed” communication boundaries?
If not, what exactly changed—and what proof supports that?

**The COOL factors !**

This challenge lets you build something that feels like a real SOC capability for IoT:

You’re not just detecting anomalies—you’re building a trust engine.
You’re not just raising alerts—you’re producing proof and reasoning.
You’re using AI/ML in a realistic, controlled way—like modern cybersecurity products do.

Welcome to the epicenter of innovation and collaboration, the D4 Community's Hackathon!

**What We Are:**
[D4 Community](https://d4community.com) is proud to present an exhilarating hackathon hosted at CGC University Mohali, where we bring together budding tech enthusiasts, aspiring innovators, and problem solvers under one roof. With a passion for technology and a drive for innovation, we're dedicated to fostering an environment where bright minds can thrive.

desc:
**NXTGEN** is a 24-hour open innovation hackathon hosted at Express Avenue Mall as part of TEXUS 2026, the flagship fest of SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Ramapuram. It brings together student innovators to think fast, collaborate intensively, and build beyond classroom boundaries.
Join our whatsapp Group:https://chat.whatsapp.com/KIc4EuZAAOyHZUc9im3jbg 
Set in a dynamic public venue, teams ideate and develop real-world solutions across diverse tracks through rapid experimentation and teamwork. More than a competition, NXTGEN is a celebration of technology, creativity, and next-generation ideas.

# Eligibility 
Open to all Under Graduate (UG) Students

# Team Formation
Participants must form teams of **2–4 members.**
**Solo participation is not allowed.**

# Important Note
This is an open innovation hackathon where teams define their own problem statements.
All ideas must align with one of the official tracks.
Plagiarism or copied ideas will result in immediate disqualification.
Teams requiring guidance or sample problem statements may contact the official hackathon team at the registered email ID.

# Competition Format
A Pre-Event Shortlisting Round will be conducted before the main hackathon.
This round will be a PPT-based idea presentation, where teams propose their own problem statement and solution under the umbrella of open innovation, aligned with the provided tracks.

**🔹 How the PPT Round Works**
Teams of 2–4 members participate.
Each team submits one PPT.
**Teams do not need a working prototype at this stage.**
Focus is on:
**Problem clarity
Innovation
Feasibility
Alignment with tracks**

📌 This is an idea validation round, not a coding round.

Teams must submit a **PPT with 6–8 slides**, strictly following the structure below:
[PPT Template](https://tinyurl.com/4unk5dc8)

✅ Shortlisting Process
**Top 60 teams are selected**
Results are communicated via email / official channels
**Shortlisted teams must confirm participation to secure their slot**

📌 Judges’ decisions will be final and binding.
📌 Key Notes for Participants

# Tracks
**EcoTech-** EcoTech Intelligence develops software for sustainability and environmental monitoring solutions. It covers air/water/agriculture monitoring, renewable energy tools like solar optimization and smart grids, carbon management for ESG, and precision farming for soil, water, and crop improvements.

**Healthcare-** Biomedical Solutions builds digital healthcare systems to boost patient outcomes, efficiency, and access. The track targets multilingual medicine, AI clinical decision support, remote monitoring, PHR platforms, and healthcare analytics for population management, hospital optimization, and automated insurance claims.

**AthleTech-** AthleTech drives software innovations for athletic performance, analytics, and fitness. The track covers community apps, fan engagement, interactive viewing, sports analytics, wellness tech like yoga, operational systems for competitions and scholarships, and nutrition tracking with localized food databases.

**Dev Velocity-** Dev Velocity emphasizes intelligent automation to accelerate business processes and software development. The track highlights developer tools, code analysis, debugging, workflow automation, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, logistics/supplier management, compliant supply chain automation, and cost-effective startup monitoring.

**VoyageTech-** VoyageTech Experience aims to transform transportation, tourism, and urban mobility with intelligent software solutions. The track covers public transport with real-time tracking and safety, smart tourism apps for monuments/cultural experiences/custom itineraries/regional cuisine, route guidance, crowd monitoring, accessibility, multimodal aggregators, and unified payments.

**FinTrust-** FinTech Fusion merges decentralized infrastructure with traditional finance for secure, transparent solutions. The track covers blockchain invoice financing, digital token creation, asset platforms with verified identity, automated microfinance, secure payments, regulatory compliance software, digital document identity verification, tax reconciliation, and transaction monitoring.

desc:
# What is Base Batches?

**Base Batches** is a program designed to help builders kickstart their businesses. 

This is your chance to get noticed, get funded, and get the support you need to bring your idea to market.

Base Batches this year will feature two dedicated tracks: 
- **Startup Track:** For early-stage teams. Generally, we’re looking for teams that are anywhere from pre-product, pre-launch, or pre-seed and have raised less than ~$250K. The top 15 teams will receive a $10K grant, acceptance to an 8-week virtual program, access to Base builder hubs, and a spot to present at Demo Day in San Francisco this May.  A minimum of 3 teams will receive a $50K investment from the Base Ecosystem Fund (subject to the fund’s diligence review).
- **Student Track:** Open to students from around the world. Teams can only include undergraduate students; however, a single team can comprise students from multiple universities. The top 5 teams will be flown to San Francisco and present during Demo Day.

This is the page for the **Startup Track**

# About the Startup Track 
The startup track is designed to support early-stage teams take their business to the next level and take center stage to present to a live audience of VCs, angels, and accelerators live from  San Francisco. 

**Application Process**

In order to be considered, interested teams must submit their application by **March 9**. Top candidates will go through an interview process:
- 1x Standard interview 
- 1x subject-matter expert interview 
- Light paper (500-word submission) 


**Virtual Program**

Admitted teams will join us for a virtual kickoff week, followed by an 8-week virtual program. Admitted teams will receive: 

- **$10k grant**: to support teams during the program 
- **Dedicated Advisor**: Each team will meet 1x per week with a dedicated advisor. 
- **Mentorship Dashboard**: Access to a dashboard with SMEs across disciplines, where they can book ad hoc.
- **Builder Hub Access**: All teams will have access to work out of the nearest builder hub during the program (SF, NYC, London, Network School) 
- **Interview Series**: Teams will be interviewed and featured on Base TV to do a deep dive into the products, token economic design, and background on their team 

# Demo Day 

All teams will then join us for Demo Day live from San Francisco. Teams will then present to a live audience with investors, VCs and accelerators who we invite to attend. A minimum of 3 teams will receive a $50K investment from the Base Ecosystem Fund (subject to the fund’s diligence review). All teams will be considered for investment by Coinbase Ventures.

name: Devfolio Student Hackathon Grants 2026
desc:
We’re launching a grant program to empower student organizers across India to host world-class hackathons on their campuses.

- 💰 Grant Amount: Tailored to your region and hackahton.
- 🎓 Who can apply: Student Organizers at universities and colleges across **[Regions]** in 2026
- ⚡ What’s included: Direct funding support, access to AWS workshops, content bundle, and environment to build your prototype.
- ✨ The Devfolio platform to streamline applications and project submissions.

But the best part? Organizers and participants will get to tap into the [AWS Builder Center](https://nsb.dev/createbuilderid), home for builders to access all builder resources, engage with the AWS community, and provide feedback or product suggestions to AWS product teams.

# How it works? 🛠️
1. Get Hackathon verified on Devfolio - Get your hackathon set up and verified on Devfolio. Our verification process is thorough and allows us to ensure all the details are available for hackers before your hackathon is announced. 

2. Apply for the grant (here) – Fill out the grant application explaining about your hackathon mission, why you want to host it, and how you’ll use the grant.
**We allow one application per hackathon.**

3. Get shortlisted – Our team will evaluate applications based on vision, scale, student impact and support scope for your hackathon. We may reach out to get more details.

4. Receive funding & support – If selected, you’ll be onboarded to our grant program which will include sponsorship + support from AWS team during your hackathon.

5. Host your hackathon – Build the event you’ve always dreamed of, with all the resources you need in place.

6. Read the FAQs - We answer most of your questions related to the program in the FAQ below, please go through all of them before applying to the program.

> There should be no conflict of interest when applying for the grants.


## Why this matters 💡
With thousands of students across India building the future, hackathons are the beating heart of the developer ecosystem. By lowering the barrier to organizing them, we’re giving more students the chance to host meaningful events and inspire their peers to build.
AWS brings global expertise and infrastructure to the table. Devfolio brings a decade of hackathon know-how. Together, we want to make it easier for the next generation of student leaders to create experiences that launch ideas, careers, and communities.

#HackOnAWS #BuildOnAWS
