desc:
# **Mandatory Hackathon Registration Link - https://forms.gle/KTeKGov1akfWrU5P7**

# Project Submission Link - 
 https://forms.gle/UTm3F9T2SKJ2BXe99

Filecoin Orbit India Hackathon is a 10 day long hackathon organized by Loarr in partnership with the Filecoin foundation with the goal of inspiring and fostering a community of builders promoting technological advancements in the Web3 space.

Packed with amazing sessions by industry experts and workshops, we invite you to grab the opportunity to interact and learn from the leading minds in the ecosystem and build secure and innovative decentralized applications for the future.

In a universe of infinite possibilities, you have 10 days to innovate, brainstorm and show us what you've got!

# **We will have the presentations starting at 4 pm on the 23rd.**


**# Guidelines for the Filecoin Orbit India Hackathon - BITS Pilani Hyd:**

**Original work:** All submissions must be the original work of the participants. Plagiarism of code or any other form of intellectual property is strictly prohibited.

**Team size:** Each team can consist of a minimum of 1 member and a maximum of 6 members. Teams can be formed in advance or at the hackathon.

**Code of Conduct:** All submissions must comply with Devfolio's Code of Conduct. Any submission that violates the Code of Conduct will be disqualified.

**Filecoin Mainnet**: All submissions must be deployed over the Filecoin Mainnet/Testnet. Participants are encouraged to use the latest version of the Filecoin network for their solutions.

**Submission deadline:** All submissions must be completed and submitted on Devfolio by April 23rd. Late submissions would not be accepted.

Problem statement: Participants are free to choose any problem statement that they want to solve. However, the solution should be related to Filecoin's decentralized storage network.

**Judging criteria:** The submissions will be judged based on the following criteria:

Innovation and creativity
Impact and scalability
Technical excellence
Use of Filecoin

**Prize pool:** The top 3 winners of the hackathon will receive a prize pool of $500 (USD 500) to help them further develop their solutions.

**Rights to solutions:** Participants will retain ownership of their solutions. However, by submitting their solutions, participants grant the organizing committee the right to showcase their solutions to the public.

We wish you the best of luck with the hackathon and hope that you have a productive and enjoyable experience!

name: ZKP Online Hackathon
desc:
Are you a ZKP enthusiast with a passion for blockchain technology? Do you have programming skills and experience in Web3 or ZKP-related open-source projects? If so, we invite you to participate in the ZKP Online Hackathon organized by Mantle and Antalpha Labs!

Coinciding with Antalpha Labs x Mantle ZKP Hacker House in Chiang Mai, this hackathon focuses on zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) technology and its potential applications. Both in-person participants from the hacker house and online participants are eligible for bounties, with Mantle offering $7.5k in bounties for projects that are deployed on their high-performance Ethereum layer-2 network with modular design, low fees & high security.

The event will provide ZKP learning materials prior to the hackathon and will feature a variety of activities such as lectures, discussions, and brainstorming sessions to help participants develop project ideas. Mentors will be available to offer technical and strategic guidance, and the event will culminate in a Demo Day to showcase the outcomes of the event to industry experts and VCs.

The event's main focus will be on applications that incorporate ZKP technology, such as games, social applications, NFT, Defi, and other related areas, as well as developer tools and infrastructure like web-based integrated development environments (IDEs) or command-line tools.

If you're interested in participating, please apply asap and start hacking!

name: Build Week
desc:
Welcome to Build Week, the flagship event of the BITS Blockchain Club, BITS Pilani! As a community of passionate Web3 enthusiasts and builders, we are excited to host a hackathon as part of Web3 Week to offer budding developers an opportunity to dive into the world of web3.

This hackathon is the perfect platform for all those looking to get hands-on experience in building with web3 technologies. Participants will have the opportunity to tackle cutting-edge challenges and create innovative solutions.

This year, the hackathon is Powered by Fabwelt, Router (official cross-chain partner), and Spheron Protocol (official hosting partner), and participants will have the chance to receive mentoring from seasoned web3 experts and participate in insightful workshops and networking events. The hackathon will be hosted on Devfolio, and our track sponsors will be Filecoin, Polygon, and Solana. The event will conclude with a pitching session where participants will present their projects to a jury of web3 experts.

We are proud to have had the support of leading companies like LearnWeb3DAO, Arcana, Biconomy, and Celo at our last year's hackathon. Our sponsors helped by providing technical workshops and offered bounties for the best projects leveraging their technology stack.

So what are you waiting for? Join us at Build Week and build the future of web3 today!

name: Filecoin Orbit India Hackathon - IIIT Sri City
desc:
Filecoin Orbit India Hackathon is a 30 day long hackathon organized by Loarr in partnership with the Filecoin foundation with the goal of inspiring and fostering a community of builders promoting technological advancements in the Web3 space.

Packed with amazing sessions by industry experts and workshops, we invite you to grab the opportunity to interact and learn from the leading minds in the ecosystem and build secure and innovative decentralized applications for the future.

In a universe of infinite possibilities, you have 30 days to innovate, brainstorm and show us what you've got!

# **Guidelines for the Filecoin Orbit India Hackathon - IIIT Sri City:**

**Original work**: All submissions must be the original work of the participants. Plagiarism of code or any other form of intellectual property is strictly prohibited.

**Team size**: Each team can consist of a minimum of 1 member and a maximum of 6 members. Teams can be formed in advance or at the hackathon.

**Code of Conduct**: All submissions must comply with Devfolio's Code of Conduct. Any submission that violates the Code of Conduct will be disqualified.

**Filecoin Mainnet**: All submissions must be deployed over the Filecoin Mainnet/Testnet. Participants are encouraged to use the latest version of the Filecoin network for their solutions.

**Submission deadline**: All submissions must be completed and submitted on Devfolio by April 16th. Late submissions would not be accepted.

**Problem statement**: Participants are free to choose any problem statement that they want to solve. However, the solution should be related to Filecoin's decentralized storage network.

**Judging criteria**: The submissions will be judged based on the following criteria:

*Innovation and creativity
Impact and scalability
Technical excellence
Use of Filecoin*

**Prize pool**: The top 3 winners of the hackathon will receive a prize pool of $500 (USD 500) to help them further develop their solutions.

**Rights to solutions**: Participants will retain ownership of their solutions. However, by submitting their solutions, participants grant the organizing committee the right to showcase their solutions to the public.

We wish you the best of luck with the hackathon and hope that you have a productive and enjoyable experience!

prizes.name: Use Moonbeam, XCM, and Manta to build a privacy-focused application on Polkadot.
prizes.desc:
# General Description of Moonbeam and Manta

Moonbeam is a smart contract platform for the Polkadot ecosystem, focused on Ethereum compatibility. It allows developers to build smart contracts for decentralized applications using Polkadot's cross-consensus messaging (XCM) technology to communicate with other parachains in the ecosystem. The XCM-Transactor pallet enables developers to craft XCM messages to execute arbitrary call data on other parachains in the ecosystem.

Manta is a privacy-focused platform built on Polkadot that provides a secure and decentralized privacy layer for multiple applications using ZK technology. The Manta SDK enables developers to submit MantaPay and zkSBT extrinsics, or craft the encoded call data for such calls, so that these extrinsics can be executed through XCM. MantaPay is a privacy-focused payment gateway that enables secure and private transactions for merchants and buyers. zkSBT allows for secure and private minting of SBTs without revealing any additional information beyond the validity of the transaction itself. This allows users to maintain segregation between their zkAddress and all other assets, including the zkSBT, that belong to said zkAddress.

# General Description of the Bounty
The goal of this bounty is to build a privacy-focused application that utilizes Manta's privacy layer and is initiated from a smart contract or decentralized application on Moonbeam. To accomplish this, developers can use both Testnet: Moonbase Alpha and Manta, which are connected via XCM.

# General Bounty Requirements
From a Moonbeam perspective, developers can use the XCM-Transactor pallet and precompile to remotely transact on Manta, either using MantaPay or working around zkSBTs. However, from a UX perspective, the application must be built on Moonbeam.

From a Manta perspective, developers must build a privacy-focused use case based on the Manta SDK, either MantaPay or zkSBT, but where the action is initiated via XCM. For MantaPay, create a payment solution that can remotely interact with another parachain. For zkSBTs, launch zkSBT on Manta and create a use case for the zkSBT that can use Proof Key to achieve walletless transactions.

# Judging Criteria
Originality & Innovation
Ease of use (UI/UX)
Technical complexity
Level of Completion

prizes.name: Cryptography bounty
prizes.desc:
In scope of this bounty we are open to submissions implementing any interesting cryptographic improvement for the shielder, as well as non-trivial applications of it. Some suggestions include:
-**Designs based on computationally limited trusted third party**: we are currently working on adding an MPC component to our frameworks, with the main goal of replacing trusted components in designs that rely upon their existence. Can you propose a non-trivial protocol, in which existence of a trusted third party is absolutely necessary, but in which the actions of such a party are limited to, say, constant number of secret multiplications per user input (additions and multiplications by public constant are cheap for MPC)? It can be either a user-facing product, or just an interesting cryptographic primitive. 

-**Guarding against bad actors:** propose a design that protects the shielder from malicious use, understood as direct money laundering. It may be a version of a recently popular idea where users can prove that none of their funds originate from the specified set of ‘bad’ addresses, or that they do originate from a prespecified set of ‘good’ addresses, without revealing the particular origin. While the inspiration for this can come from the recently discussed Tornado Cash improvements, we would be happy to see also alternative designs and ideas achieving similar goals.

name: Dev Hacks
desc:
**Checkout [Technival Website](https://technival.netlify.app/) for offline events happening in TECHNIVAL 7.O**

**Join Discord: [Discord Invite Link](https://discord.gg/puT4AJ3Z)**

Alone we can do so little, together we can do so much. 
Get ready because for today you and your team have to think of an idea to work with. Your objective is that you have to choose an idea for a product that could tackle a problem due to which these goals were created. Think about what kind of problem your product could solve, who it would benefit, and how it could make a positive impact on a global scale.

**What is Dev Hacks?**

Dev Hacks is Technival’s Hackathon event which is happening for the first time ever in Kirori Mal college, which is amongst the top 10 colleges in DU.

Fun fact: TECHNIVAL is being held offline for the first time in 3 years but Dev Hacks is being held online so as people have the choice to work from the comfort of their home as well

**Why should we participate?**

Well particularly there are 3 reasons  on why you should participate in Dev Hacks 

- Dev Hacks is an event where participants will have something to gain out at the end. They will learn something new and would carry it forward with them.

- Our event is going to be huge and winning it will mean even bigger so it will be something you will be able to add in your list of experiences or also on LinkedIn

- You will also have a chance to network with your fellow peers and with the core team of our society organizing the event.

**How will the projects be judged?**

- **Originality**: Participants will be judged on how original yet fresh, something which is out of the box yet feasible. Plagiarism shall not be tolerated and would lead to immediate disqualification.

- **Social Impact**:  Extra Brownie points shall be awarded if your project is helping solve a large scale world issue while being possible to implement and being economically and technologically feasible.

- **Technicalities**: Technical expertise will be a significant factor in evaluating your project. Did you incorporate advanced techniques such as MLOps, integrating Node.js with Python, or utilizing Docker for deployment purposes? Your project's technical proficiency will be considered in the assessment.

- **Market readiness**: While it may be difficult to create a market-ready project within the timeframe of a hackathon, extra points may be awarded for projects that are close to being fully deployed and usable. If you have created a website, have you deployed it? If you have built an Android application, have you included the release APK file on GitHub?

- **Experience**: Finally, regardless of your level of experience, what did you learn during the hackathon? Did you push yourself to try new things and expand your skills? Or did you create something you were already familiar with? Learning is highly valued, and it is important for all participants to feel that they have gained something from the experience.

**Guidelines**
- Copying code from the internet is common practice, but it is important to give credit where credit is due. This means properly attributing any code that was copied in the README file of your project. It is not necessary to attribute documentation, but if you are using logic from a StackOverflow answer or other source, you should give credit to the original author.

- It is crucial to maintain a realistic git commit history. We will be reviewing your commit history to ensure that you are using ethical development practices. If you commit all of your code at once, this is suspicious and may result in disqualification. However, if you have a history of many commits with clear development progression, this is a good sign that you are following proper procedures.

- Your project should include a README.md file that explains the various aspects of your project.

- In order to be considered for the hackathon, your project must be open-sourced on GitHub.

- To submit your project, you must use Devfolio as your submission platform.

Devcation'23 is a week-long technical festival organized by Google Developer Student Clubs - Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women that celebrates diversity in the TechForGood Domain. 

During the week, we have the Devcation'23 hackathon with two tracks:
1. Design & Solve
2. Hack & Solve

1. Ideating Solutions
2. Logo Making


Along with this, we will have various knowledge-imparting and super fun recreational sessions. This event will act as a platform to attain knowledge and collaborate on projects and gain mentorship from the experts. It will help beginners to kickstart their technical journey!

Our aim is to inspire, challenge and motivate passionate innovators, especially women, to pursue their careers in Technology and develop solutions to current world problems. We believe that together we can make a difference. Participants will get opportunities to build sustainable products under the guidance of our skilled mentors. They will not only get a chance to learn and explore new tech stacks but also network over fun team-building activities.

Join us at Devcation'23 to learn, create and build together!

name: EduHack 1.0
desc:
**EduMinerva** is organizing **EduVation**, which comprises a hackathon **EduHack** that aims to develop real-life and practical solutions to serious issues and problems. The event focuses on the use of technology to cater to various needs and requirements in large and life-affecting domains of the tech world and society. The competition will require participants to think outside of the box, leave their comfort zones and idealize and implement solutions that can bring about real change and development. 
The theme of the event is ***Beyond All Limits***.


**EVENT DETAILS**

**Round-1**
The participant's problem-solving approach and thought process will be tested in this round. The online submission shall take place. Teams work on the problem statements, mold their solutions accordingly, and make a demonstration video/PPT submission. Judging will be completely based on your abstract submission. This round involves: Detailed Abstract submission (150-200 words) 

**Judging Round**
Teams are filtered on the basis of their idea and their previous submissions.

**Round-2**
This will be an offline round, for the teams which get shortlisted from the results of Round 1. It shall be the final round where each shortlisted team will have to code, implement and present their solution. The practicality, uniqueness, business awareness, and relevance of the theme will be tested for each solution presented in this round: Most importantly, technical solutions to real-life problems are encouraged

**Round-3**
The qualifiers of Round 2 will have to deliver an offline presentation in front of our judges. The final winner of this round shall be declared the winner of the hackathon. 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/799cdb6b8d5a4d8ea3a4d384433a74d7/934a28c1-4605-4f92-b223-aca4c3b7ac6a.png)

The winners will be announced in the closing ceremony at the venue.

**Rulebook**

All participants are requested to join the discord channel for further updates.

name: Quasar
desc:
**For uploading your presentation, click **[here](https://forms.gle/mvv4gcevJ81vNwZGA)**!**

**A sample PPT template for the idea submission stage is given** [**here**](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1kKQNZp1DlOA6mUHuN2p0FeoyQneh2bBZ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=101097554948121542601&rtpof=true&sd=true).


Quasar is the flagship annual 24-hour hackathon organized by Vasantdada Patil Pratishthan's College of Engineering & Visual Arts wherein young innovators and developers from all over the country come together to find alarming problems in various sectors and brainstorm their solutions to said problems and showcase their true potential to the alarming problems of the region & the world. It is completely organized by a team of dedicated students and also consists of a series of workshops and other fun activities to make the stay memorable.

We are excited to announce our upcoming first rendition of Quasar to be in a hybrid mode, designed for beginners with a passion for innovation and sustainability. Our event will feature multiple themes, allowing participants to submit their ideas in the given PPT format and showcase their creativity offline in VPPCOE&VA.

**For uploading your presentation, click **[here](https://forms.gle/mvv4gcevJ81vNwZGA)**!**

# **Dates:**
25th February - 12th March, 2023. (Registration)
13th March - 18th March, 2023. (Online Phase 1)
25th March - 26th March, 2023. (Offline Hackathon)

# **Prizes:**
We have a prize pool worth **₹60,000** and more to offer!

# **Sectors:**
**Agriculture/Rural Development:** Whether you're interested in creating tools for better crop management or finding ways to increase access to markets for small-scale farmers, this sector offers a wide range of possibilities for you to showcase your skills and make a positive impact on the world.

**Smart Education:** This sector provides an opportunity for you to explore innovative solutions for the education industry, from improving access to quality education for all, to developing cutting-edge educational technologies.

**MediTech/BioTech:** Whether you're interested in using AI for disease diagnosis or creating wearable devices for monitoring health, the possibilities for innovation in this sector are endless.

**Smart City:** In this sector, we're looking for innovative ideas that can make our cities more sustainable, connected, and efficient. Whether it's developing smart traffic management systems, enhancing public transportation, or creating solutions for waste management, we're looking for solutions that can improve the quality of life for citizens.

# **Phase Details:**
**Phase 1:** Based on the 4 sectors given to you, the participants need to choose a sector and based on that sector, the team to formulate the problem statement and the technology solution to the chosen problem statement. As part of this problem statement and the technology solution, the team has to prepare a PowerPoint Presentation and submit the same during the process of registration. Once your registration is complete, you will receive a mail stating that we have received your registration. After registration, the participating teams have to submit a video stating the reason of your participation and why you have chosen this sector and particular problem statement.

**A sample PPT template for the idea submission stage is given** [**here**](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1kKQNZp1DlOA6mUHuN2p0FeoyQneh2bBZ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=101097554948121542601&rtpof=true&sd=true).

**Phase 2:** We will evaluate your problem statement and solution and after that the participating teams will be given confirmation of your participation on March 18, 2023. Means, at this juncture you will officially become a part of Quasar.

**Phase 3:** This phase will start with your presence at the venue on March 25, 2023 at 2.00 p.m. To begin with, the judges will look into your problem statement and technology solution to it. The judges will suggest some implementation changes in your stated technology solution. You need to incorporate the changes suggested by the judges into your solution in the next 24-hours, means till March 26, 2.00 p.m.

**Phase 4:** Based on the judges’ perspective and decision, some teams will be shortlisted for the final round. After that, before the jury, problem statement, its technology solution and the implementation will be bound in a business idea. The best teams shortlisted from your business ideas will be declared as winners of the hackathon.

# **Venue:**
Vasantdada Patil Pratishthan's College of Engineering & Visual Arts, Sion, Mumbai - 400022, Maharashtra.

name: HackMol 4.0
desc:
# What is Hackmol
HackMOL is the flagship annual 30-hour
hackathon being organized by Google Developer
Student Club (GDSC) of NIT Jalandhar wherein
young coders & developers from all over the
country join together to build projects & solutions
to the alarming problems of the region & the world.
It is organized at the end of Month of Learning
(MOL), a series of workshops & seminars focused
and centered around the latest technologies.


Over the years HackMOL has established itself as
the Biggest Hackathon of Punjab with a awe-inspiring
attendance of over 700+, 1100+ & 1300+
hackers in successive editions but this year
HackMOL has advanced to another level by serving
as the premier and the opening event of Techniti (the
annual Tech Fest of NIT Jalandhar) with
anticipation of over 2000+ hackers joining us

We are excited to announce our upcoming hackathon in **Hybrid Mode** designed for beginners with a passion for innovation and sustainability. Our event will feature multiple themes, allowing participants to submit their ideas in the [given PPT format](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QzHO19C7BRt7Lsec8OS0GSaMTiQMhdcMqeIYp1uM6fs/edit#slide=id.p) and showcase their creativity offline in NITJ.

# Structure of Hackathon
The Hackathon is going to be conducted to two Phases

## **Round 1**
The participants are required to come up with an idea and submit the PPT on the Devfolio Platform.
The selected student would be given the Invitation to join Round 2 taking Place offline at NIT Jalandhar.

## PPT Format Link
 [PPT format](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QzHO19C7BRt7Lsec8OS0GSaMTiQMhdcMqeIYp1uM6fs/edit#slide=id.p) 

## Timeline for the Round 1
1. **Registration Starts** : 14 January 2023
2. **Last Date for Team Registration** : 5th February 2023
3. **Last date for PPT submission** : 10th February
4. **Round 1 Results** : 15th February

## **Round 2**
The invited teams are required to come up with the working prototypes of their project within 48 hours from the moment Hackathon starts.

## Timeline for Round 2
1. **Round 2 Registration** : *TBA*
2. **Hackathon Kickoff** : 25th February 2023
3. **Hackathon Ends** : 26th February 2023

# Facilities Provided for Offline Hackathon
1. Full-night stay with proper bedding
2. Internet Facility 24/7
3. Proper temperature-controlled rooms.
4. Food and Refreshment for the whole Hackathon period







# Themes you can choose from 
(but not limited to the following)

1. **Green Technology**
2. **Blockchain/Decentralized app(Dapp) Development (Web3)**
3. **Agriculture and Rural Development**
4. **MedTech/Healthcare**
5. **Machine Learning / Artificial Intelligence**
6. **Smart Education**
7. **CyberSecurity**
8. **Internet of Things (IoT)**
NEW IDEAS WELCOMED
OPEN INNOVATION IDEAS in software or hardware for a better future ahead! (Beginner Friendly)

# **Announcements**
1. Allowed Team Size : 1-4
*Team Size of 1-5 was create by mistake, forgive us*

- Selected teams will be invited to the campus to participate in a 36-hour hackathon.

- Teams will have access to resources and support from the Machine Learning Club.
- The final presentations will be judged by a panel of experts and prizes will be awarded to the top teams.

name: Flow Hackathon
desc:
# [THIS HACKATHON FINISHED! CHECK OUT THE NEW FLOW HACKATHON HAPPENING JUNE 15 - JULY 15](https://flow.com/hackathon)


---


This hackathon is all about **building innovative on-chain experiences #onFlow, and reaching mainstream audiences**. Thanks to Flow’s frictionless onboarding, on-chain scalability and revolutionary smart contract programming language (Cadence), on-chain experiences don’t need to be limited to a mint. Whether you’re looking to build a mobile game, a DeFi application or building experiences on top of existing apps like NBA TopShot, this hackathon is for you!

**But that’s not all! Great submissions will qualify for our post-hackathon launchpad**

Following the traditional hackathon phase, all qualifying submissions can enter a 2 month long launchpad to receive support to get to production on mainnet. This Launchpad phase will consist of technical mentorship, privileged access to millions in funding, networking and marketing.

**This hackathon has one primary track dedicated to building innovative on-chain logic aimed at a mainstream audience.** This means you can build anything you want; your guiding principle should be: would your friends enjoy using this app, even if they don’t know anything about web3?


Unlike most hackathons, the Flow Hackathon is a unique event where great ideas can make it all the way to mainnet. The hackathon will happen in the following phases:
- **Phase 1 – Education Series (February 10-20):** Learn from world class blockchain and Web3 experts. Form teams and get ready to start building on the most scalable Layer 1 blockchain.
- **Phase 2 – Build Sprint (February 21-26):** This is the time to work on a prototype and deploy it to testnet. Join us from anywhere in the world virtually or at one of our sprint locations. The submission window will close on February 26. Prizes and awards will be on February 28.
- **Phase 3 – Launchpad (March - April):** Following the hackathon, the best ideas will enter a two-month launchpad where project teams can get support to reach mainnet and take their app mainstream (e.g. mentorship from top exponents in Web3, priority access to grants and venture funding).

### For more info refer **[Flow Hackathon Guide](https://flowhackathon.notion.site/Flow-Hackathon-Guide-b902f1c353ea4989b5d69ce266b588b9)**.

name: RapidHacks
desc:
Rapid Hacks is a 24-hour online hackathon organized by GDSC IGDTUW, with tracks designed specifically for beginners. No matter if you are still ideating your solution, designing it or have a prototype ready ~ Everyone is invited!

The hackathon has tracks designed specially for beginners with no-code, low-code and coding tracks:

 IDEATE TRACK: The hackers can submit their idea.
 DESIGN TRACK: The hackers have to present a design of what their solution would look like.
 SOLVE TRACK: The hackers have to present a solution to the problem statement that they have chosen.
The theme for Rapid Hacks is building Sustainable Technology. However, the hackers can also submit projects based on any other theme under the Open Innovation Category.


TIMELINE
The hacking period is of 24-hours starting from 12:00 Noon IST, 18th February 2023 to 12:00 Noon IST, 19th February 2023. 

 11:00 AM: Opening Ceremony: Hacking period starts
 12:00 Noon: Hacking Period Ends
 7:00 PM: Closing Ceremony

The results for all the events will be announced during the closing ceremony.

Also add a governance mechanism for the holders of fractions to vote on any related propositions to the NFT such as when to sell, whom to sell etc. Price of each fraction can be proportional to the current floor price of the original edition. Think of fractional.art but on Tezos.

name: Reckon 4.0
desc:
RECKON 4.0 is sun city's most innovative hackathon, where developers, entrepreneurs, and technology enthusiasts get an opportunity to create the best possible solutions within 36 hours to emerging issues via this platform 
## **How to get ourselves Registered At Reckon 4.0?**
**Step1:** Register yourself by clicking on the **Apply Now** button and fill in all the required details.
**Step 2:**  Create your own team or join an existing team(as this is a team-based event).
**Step 3:** Reckon4.0 team will accept your registration and then will give an RSVP link to the registered mail id then after all the steps are completed as mentioned in the mail, you will be able to submit a solution on any problem statements.
## **Why Should I join?**
Reckon 4.0 some say is the same as others, but What’s different from its previous versions,
 So here it is, This time we are Aiming and motivated to give our participants not only a hackathon but a journey from which they’ll get a  life-long learning experience,  where you’ll meet a large number of tech-Savy such as profound developers, designers, entrepreneurs and especially students and professionals, who are interested in technology and problem-solving as much as you are. For many of us, it will be a Once in lifetime opportunity to visit the royal city Of “MARWAR”, and get a chance to grab your hands on the Immense prize pool of 4 lakhs !!! and much more.
So, what are you waiting for register yourselves today and be a part of this Looming Journey Of CREATION.
## **How will the projects be judged?**
The projects will be judged on the basis of the following criteria:

**Innovation:** How can someone not think of innovation while building a project in the Cluster Innovation Centre? We will be judging how innovative your project is. Does your project already exist somewhere on the internet? If yes, how is it different from the existing ones? Is it solving a problem more efficiently? Or is it a completely new idea?

**Originality:** How original is your project idea? We all copy code from the internet, but does your project consist only of copied code?

**Social impact:** How about helping humankind with your project? Is your project limited to programmers or will it be impacting our society in a positive way? Everyone loves projects which are aimed at social good.

Technicalities: We will obviously be judging your project on how technically great it is. Maybe you created a CI/CD pipeline for your project? Or, binded Rust with Python? Or, used Docker in the deployment process?

**Market readiness:** We know, it is quite impossible to create a project that is market ready in 36 hours, but, this will earn you extra points! Created a website? DEPLOY IT! An Android application? ADD THE RELEASE APK FILE TO GITHUB RELEASES!

**How much did you learn?:** Is this your first hackathon and you ended up creating a full stack project with an automated deployment pipeline? Or, is this your nth hackathon and you created a project that you are very familiar with? Learning always pays off, and we don't want beginners to feel intimidated by experienced hackers!
## **What’s Free…?**
The main question is what’s not, everything is “FREE OF COST” our Aim is to truly give our participants the “Hassle-free” experience for whom they registered for 
Starting with the FREE travel journey, FREE Accommodation, and FREE Food including all the main course meals, starters, snacks, Energy drinks, and much more. And last but not least the “WorthWhile” Experience Which we all deserve .
## **Where can I find the Problem Statements?**
So, this is the most important question, you can find all the Problem Statements under the prize section above ⬆
## **Hackathon Details -**
Reckon 4.0 will be held in two phases-
### **PHASE 1: Solution Submission Round (Online)**
it's going to be an online round where you will register your team and will submit a solution for any of the listed problem statements
## **—---------------(Top 100 Teams  Will Be Shortlisted)------------**

### **Phase 2: 36-hour Hackathon(offline)**
It's the final round of the hackathon, this will be a physical round at JIET Jodhpur, Top 100 Shortlisted teams will be called here in offline mode to compete in a 36-hour-crazy hackathon.

**Final Judgment round** - final Participants will go through 3 judgment round 
The judgment rounds will be based on some criteria and it will be done by industry experts and domain specialists.

prizes.desc:
# Predict the Segment - Hotstar
**Description:** Determining the demographics of customers is one of the most key tasks in the advertising domain. Advertisers usually want to target customers based on demographic attributes. However, it is difficult to get demographic data from all the customers since
that can add friction to the user experience.
- At Hotstar, we have detailed information on all the content that customers watch, let’s call it “watch patterns” and we’d like to use this signal to fine tune demo-targeting.
We are seeking a machine learning based solution using which we can learn patterns from customers whose watch patterns are already known. In this competition, the task is to generate predictive models that can best capture the behavior. Participants are free to use any open source external data.
**Data Set Information:**
A zipped file containing train, test and sample submission files are given. The training dataset consists of data corresponding to 200,000 customers and the test dataset consists of 100,000 customers. Both training and test data is in the form of json dict, where key is masked user ID and value is an aggregation of all records corresponding to the user as described below:
Description ID: a unique identifier 
titles: titles of the shows watched by the user and watch_time on different titles in the format “title:watch_time” separated by comma, e.g. “JOLLY LLB:23, Ishqbaaz:40”. 
watch_time is in seconds 
genres: same format as titles
cities: same format as titles
tod: total watch time of the user spreaded across different time of days (24 hours format) in the format time_of_day:watch_time” separated by comma, e.g. “1:454, “17”:5444”.
dow: total watch time of the user spreaded across different days of week (7 days format) in the format “day_of_week:watch_time” separated by comma, e.g. “1:454, “6”:5444” 
segment target variable, consider them as interest segments. 
For modeling, encode pos = 1, neg = 0
Download dataset from here
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YPVPife9QCCQPBcT5yOYi-gCpV6NABMR/view
**Helpful techniques**
- Try different clustering techniques to segment users and use those outputs as features to your machine learning models.
- Data cleaning and feature creation should be novel. Go with your intuition.

# ATM is not as secure as it should be.
**Description:** While doing transactions through ATM a question pops out in our mind is our money secured or what would happen if someone tries to do the transaction without permission. So basically in an Automated teller machine if we insert an ATM card and we know the pin so we can take out the money no matter if we are the true owner of that card or not. So there can be cases of robbery, stealing cards, getting the pin information and as a result, a person can lose all his/her money.
**Exact Problem:** So in order to prevent such cases of peculation what we can do is, we can insert an additional step to complete the transaction and that would be installing a fingerprint scanner and camera. We will try to make a network of trusted people which will include a group of 5 and those 5 will be able to do transactions from a particular card, no one else can do it and if someone else tries to do so, and fails to get his/her fingerprint matched then automatically a message will be sent to the owner.

name: HashHacks 5
desc:
**Don't forget to join our Discord server linked below! HashHacks will be conducted in hybrid mode, that is, you can join us offline at DU overnight, or submit your project remotely.**

## What will I do at HashHacks?

One task. One team. 24 hours. Break free of all bounds and develop something exciting. Something innovative. Something which has the ability to create a better world!

Code your way through this 24 hours hackathon where you focus your time, energy, and enthusiasm on building a product or service which can help create change. Because, using good software feels good. But building one feels even better!

## What is HashHacks?

HashHacks is CIC's flagship hackathon, conducted under Convoke, CIC's annual Tech Fest. You would be surprised to know that CIC is Delhi University's only engineering college, and it is an amazing place for coders, musicians, researchers, and even photographers! HashHacks and Convoke are being organized after 3 whole pandemic years, and we promise, you won't go back disappointed.

## Why should I join?

Join us {offline, online} for prizes valued at over Rs. 3 lakhs, cloud credits, swags, merch, internship/full-time opportunities, free snacks, FREE COFFEE, and unlimited FUN + LEARNING! We hope to see you at CIC, DU's only engineering college!

## What about the theme and the mode?

HashHacks will be conducted in a hybrid mode! HashHacks is also open theme, that is, we will accept a diverse range of projects! 

## How will the projects be judged?

The projects will be judged on the basis of the following criteria:

1. **Innovation**: How can someone not think of innovation while building a project in the Cluster **Innovation** Centre? We will be judging how innovative your project is. Does your project already exist somewhere on the internet? If yes, how is it different from the existing ones? Is it solving a problem more efficiently? Or is it a completely new idea?

2. **Originality**: How original is your project idea? We all copy code from the internet, but does your project consist only of copied code?

3. **Social impact**: How about helping humankind with your project? Is your project limited to programmers or will it be impacting our society in a positive way? Everyone loves projects which are aimed at social good.

4. **Technicalities**: We will obviously be judging your project on how technically great it is. Maybe you created a CI/CD pipeline for your project? Or, binded Rust with Python? Or, used Docker in the deployment process?

5. **Market readiness**: We know, it is quite impossible to create a project that is market ready in 24 hours, but, this will earn you extra points! Created a website? DEPLOY IT! An Android application? ADD THE RELEASE APK FILE TO GITHUB RELEASES!

6. **How much did you learn?**: Is this your first hackathon and you ended up creating a full stack project with an automated deployment pipeline? Or, is this your nth hackathon and you created a project that you are very familiar with? Learning always pays off, and we don't want beginners to feel intimidated by experienced hackers!

## Project guidelines

1. We all copy code, and it is totally fine to copy someone else's code. But, you must attribute the copied code in the README file of your project. Should you attribute documentation? No. Should you attribute a logic written by someone else as a StackOverflow answer? Yes!

2. You must maintain a realistic git commit history. We will be going through your commit history to catch any malpractices. Did you commit the complete code in one go? That is very suspicious and we might disqualify your project. You made 100 commits with a really messed up commit history? Now that sounds like a realistic development cycle!

3. Your project must have a README.md file explaining bits and pieces of your project.

4. Your project must be open-sourced on GitHub.

5. Your project must be submitted through Devfolio.

## I have more questions

Please refer to the FAQs to know more about the specifics of HashHacks. We have populated the FAQs extensively. Convoke's website (with the schedule) can be found [here](https://clusterinnovationcentre.github.io/convoke/2023/).
location: Cluster Innovation Centre, University of Delhi, GC Narang Road, Delhi, India

We are the community who are connected with our audience in both online and offline mode to keep the community growing and planning to have the hackathons, coding contests and Developers Conference. 

**Why attend hackathons?**

Everyone needs an arena to demonstrate your coding prowess. You don’t mind missing out on sleep. You also don’t mind subsisting on pizza and flat soda for 36 hours. Most importantly, you want an opportunity to participate in an event that really brings your local developer community together: you’ll meet fellow hackers, see what they’re up to, and show what you can do.

**Themes:**

-	Heritage & cultural
-	Open Innovation
-	Agriculture
-	Transportation
-	Environment & Sustainable Development Goal
-	Smart City and Infrastructure
-	Accessibility and Disability
-	Healthcare
-	Women Safety


**Eligibility Criteria**

•	Hackathon is open to all Indian science, technology and engineering students 
•	All team members must be enrolled in any courses (Graduate or post graduate). 
•	Team members can be from different academic years or colleges
•	Team members could be from any of the technology streams or any field.
•	Once teams have registered, changes in team members will not be encouraged.
•	Team size will be from 3 to 5 members.
•	Professionals are also eligible to participate.

**APPLICATION BUILDING CRITERIA:** 

•	The projects should not be pre-built. 
•	A team cannot reuse or resubmit previously submitted projects. 
•	Project should not have any threatening, inappropriate or offensive content. 
•	There should be proper documentation of the code.
•	Project should relate to some real life problem and their solution.

**DOMAIN AREAS OF HACKATHON:**

-	AI
-	Machine Learning
-	Mobile Security
-	Video Analytics
-	Web Technologies
-	Mobile computing
-	Cyber Security
-	IoT (Internet of Things)
-	Digital Forensics
-	Cybersecurity
-	Android Development (Kotlin /Java / Flutter)

prizes.name: Bounty Prize
prizes.desc:
Bounty topic: Support starknet platform #72

Description:
ProofService is a zero-trust identity binding protocol. We have a reference implementation called [proof_server(https://github.com/nextdotid/proof_server).

The binding relationship between a web2 identity and ProofService’s web3 identity (called Avatar) is done through cryptography signing and “Proof Post” mechanism.

We want to support as many platforms as possible. This is where we need your help to extend our reach to more platforms.

starknet's address format: 0xHEXSTRING_32_BYTES (compressed public key?).

Which is different from ethereum's 0xHASH_OF_PUBKEY_20_BYTES.

So starknet platform is not duplicated with current ethereum
platform, and worth supporting.

Expected outcomes
validators/starknet should be provided, both implementation and unit tests.

Signature verifying procedure should only rely on signatures generated
by starknet identity in starknet's wallet app.

You should figure out which signing algorithm is popular among
starknet community and wallets, and use it in our verifying
workflow.

Resources: https://github.com/NextDotID/proof_server/issues/72
                       https://github.com/orgs/NextDotID/projects/4?pane=issue&itemId=19746244

prizes.name: Bounty Prize
prizes.desc:
**Bounty Topics**
1. A nostr client or relay that integrate .bit system
2. An SBT system based on DIDs(.bit) rather than addresses.
3. A decentralized personal bio using .bit

**Bounty Details**
**A nostr client or relay that integrate .bit system**
Nostr is very popular these days, it's a very simple yet scalable messaging protocal. However, when you want to follow someone or want someone to follow you, you have to deal with a 32-Chars length pubkey, which is difficult to understand and hard to identify.
Luckily, we can make this process easy by using DIDs like .bit. You can set your nostr pubkey in .bit and tell your friends to follow your .bit account rather than your nostr pubkey.
However, there isn't any client that integrate .bit. So to improve the user experience, we need a nostr client intergrating .bit and resolve the profile.nostr records.

**An SBT system based on DIDs(.bit) rather than addresses.**
It is well known that the popular SBT systems currently in use are address-centered. However, this system faces many problems, including:
- Difficult to identify and remember
- Address and private key binding
- Occupies resources and costly on the chain
However, if SBT is distributed with DID as the core, these problems will be solved.

**A decentralized personal bio using .bit**
Please construct a decentralized bio web page (like Linktree) using .bit.
The page should be user-controlled and managed without relying on any centralized organizations.
The user should be able to add and delete links with an easy-to-use interface.

prizes.desc:
`Track POS bridge, Stargate, Celer, Wormhole, Socket(Bungee), Multichain, Connext`

Building a cumulative bridge inflow and outflow indicator on Polygon can be useful for several reasons:

1. Transparency and Audibility: By monitoring the cumulative inflow and outflow of tokens on a bridge, you can gain a better understanding of the liquidity on the bridge, and the health of the ecosystem. This can help to increase transparency and audibility, which can attract more users and investors to the network.
2. Price Discovery: By monitoring the cumulative inflow and outflow of tokens, you can gain insight into the demand for tokens on the bridge, which can help to inform your trading decisions and help you to identify potential price movements.
3. Risk Management: By monitoring the cumulative inflow and outflow of tokens, you can identify potential liquidity risks and take steps to mitigate them. This can help to protect your assets and reduce the likelihood of losing money due to liquidity issues.
4. Arbitrage Opportunities: By monitoring the cumulative inflow and outflow of tokens, you can identify potential arbitrage opportunities and take advantage of them to earn a profit.
5. Development: By monitoring the cumulative inflow and outflow of tokens, you can gain insight into the usage of the bridge and its development progress, this can help you to identify areas that need improvement and propose new features that can increase the bridge's usage and adoption.

[Ethereum↔Polygon Bridge | Polygon Wiki](https://wiki.polygon.technology/docs/develop/ethereum-polygon/getting-started)

prizes.name: Best Sybil Resistant Airdrop Tool
prizes.desc:
Polygon ID is a decentralized identity protocol that allows users to create a unique and verifiable identity on the Ethereum blockchain. By integrating Polygon ID into your dApp, you can ensure that each user has a unique identity and can be held accountable for their actions. This can help to prevent Sybil attacks by limiting the ability of attackers to create multiple fake identities.

Additionally, Polygon ID also allows you to perform various KYC/AML checks on the user's identity, which can further increase the security of your dApp by preventing bad actors from accessing your platform.

Overall, integrating Polygon ID into your dApp can help to improve the security and integrity of your platform by making it more resistant to Sybil attacks.

- [Introduction to Polygon ID and Self Sovereign Identity](https://rise.articulate.com/share/6yVef384BAU9-yEzMh4Qq9XGK0Hoxitf#/)

- [Polygon ID Documentation & Tutorials](https://0xpolygonid.github.io/tutorials/)

name: ETHIndia Fellowship 3.0
tagline: Join the next wave of Web3 devs who build to learn.
desc:
The much-awaited ETHIndia Fellowship is back with the post-Merge spirit this winter!

The ETHIndia Fellowship 3.0 is an 8-week mentor-led program with 2 parallel tracks. Both tracks are open to all individuals.

**Track Wei** is for a select set of top Web2 devs with a knack for learning about Web3. This track aims to familiarise them with the technology and tools required to transition to Web3 with the help of training and mentoring.

**Track Gwei** is for intermediate Web3 developers who want to go all-in and focus solely on building projects. The fellowship will provide mentorship as well as a launchpad for the development of production-level tools and products in the Web3 space.

No matter the track, you’ll get to extend your skills, get trained in the area of your interests, and receive rewards based on your future potential to do amazing work, all while making a lasting impact on the Ethereum ecosystem.

# **Timeline**

- **Applications begin:** 6:00 PM IST | 14-11-2022
- **Applications end:** 11:59 PM IST | 17-01-2023
- **Interview invites sent:** 30-12-2022 (Rolling)
- **Interviews:** 02-01-2023 → 22-01-2023
- **Final cohort announcement:**  8:00 PM IST | 22-01-2023
- **Program Starts:** 8:00 PM IST | 03-02-2023
- **Program Ends:** 8:00 PM IST | 02-04-2023

name: CYBER SHADEZ 2023
tagline: A TechFest for students to showcase their technical skills
desc:
Cyber Shadez is a technical event for undergraduate and graduate students, featuring the "TECHATHON" event. This year, the theme for the TECHATHON is cyber security, and students are encouraged to incorporate security features into their software or hardware solutions. Participants are free to use any technology or equipment they choose in the implementation process. The competition requires students to demonstrate the functionality and societal impact of their idea through multiple rounds of competition. Join us at Cyber Shadez to showcase your skills and innovation in the field of cyber security!

## Referral Program: 

![image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Fn7q51XaYAIT2yb?format=jpg&name=medium)
Join the Cyber Shadez Techathon for a chance to win big! With prizes worth Rs 1.25 lakh up for grabs.

And now, we're launching our “Referral reward program”.

So bring your friends along and earn even more worth 10k. Get started now!

Track your position: [https://cybershadez-23.devfolio.co/leaderboard](https://cybershadez-23.devfolio.co/leaderboard)

# Rules
- The Techathon is open to all students currently enrolled in a UG or PG degree program at any college or university approved by appropriate regulatory authorities.

- Teams can have a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 members.

- All the team members must COMPULSORY register for the Techathon via the Devfolio platform.

- The code developed during the Techathon must be original and cannot be taken from external sources.

- The code developed during the Techathon must be hosted using an open source platform.

- The external libraries or frameworks (if any) used in the submission must be properly credited.

- The final submission will be evaluated by judges at the end of the Techathon.

- All team members must be present during the evaluation.

- The required work must be completed within the allotted time frame of the Techathon.

- The judges decision will be considered as final in determining the winners of the Techathon.

- The top 10 submissions will be invited to present their work offline in-campus events happening on 24th and 25th Feb 2023.

- Plagiarism or cheating of any kind will not be tolerated and will result in immediate disqualification.

- By participating in the Techathon, teams give CodeCrafters Club and FCAIT, GLS University the right to use, distribute and change any materials produced during the event.

- CodeCrafters Club and FCAIT, GLS University holds the right to modify the above rules as and when needed.

name: Bit n Build
tagline: National Level Hackathon By Google Developers Student Clubs
desc:
Google Developer Student Clubs of  **Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering** and **Usha Mittal Institute of Technology** in collaboration with Google Developer Groups (GDG MAD, GDG Cloud Mumbai) will be conducting a **24-hour National Level Offline Hackathon**, "**Bit N Build**".

**Date:** 
21st - 24th Of January 2023. (Idea Submission) 
                 28th and 29th of January 2023.(Offline Hackathon)


**Venue:**
 Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering, Bandra

The aim of this hackathon is to develop technical awareness and all-round development. Additionally, we intend to accelerate a sense of learning and collaborating as a team.

**EVENT DETAILS**

**Round-1**

The team's problem-solving approach and thought process will be tested in this round. Teams can work on the problem statements, mould their solutions, and make a PPT submission. Judging will be  based on your abstract submission. The template for the same is here :- 
[Click here to view](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bXbNyVXFEINvOFxrpTWED49htCKp7wtM/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106792819085541836540&rtpof=true&sd=true)
Submit your idea in this form:-
[Click here to fill the **Form**](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFlDPYamyvCraG2fUpGPqNQfzaXtLQs3fL4k-HqCgGKoAHtw/viewform?usp=sharing)

The Problem Statements 
[Click here to view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16p3YSjIEZmOEMOiT0DOixuiAb527f1hG/view?usp=sharing) 

**Judging Round**

Teams are filtered on the basis of their idea submissions.

**Round-2**

This will be an offline round, for the teams which are shortlisted from the results of Round 1. where each shortlisted team will have to code, implement and present their solution. The practicality, uniqueness, business awareness, and relevance of their application will be tested in this round: Most importantly, technical solutions to real-life problems are encouraged.

**Round-3**

The qualified teams of Round 2 will have to deliver an offline presentation in front of our judges. The final winners of this round shall be declared as the winners of the hackathon.

name: Hackoverflow 2.0 (Phase-1)
desc:
**Submission deadline has been extended. New Deadline: 30th January 9:00 am!**

**Sample solution repository**: https://github.com/hackoverflow2/Solution-Template

For your **Project Submission** to be considered **valid** and **complete**, the following **specifications** must be ensured by each of the team/participants: 
1. Submission of the GitHub link with your project code.
2. Submission of the Demo video of your solution of not more than 3 minutes. Submissions with videos more than 3 minutes long will not be considered. 
3. Addition of the key features to the readme file as well as the appropriate field on the Devfolio portal specified under the project details.
4. You need to explicitly mention which problem statement you’ve chosen to solve, in the description of your solution on your GitHub readme and on devfolio. 
If you do not mention the problem statement, your submission will not be confirmed!

The problem statements are live at:

https://github.com/hackoverflow2/Hackoverflow-2.0

**Hackoverflow 2.0** is a week-long, AI-centric technical celebration scheduled from **23rd to 31st January 2023**, being conducted in a hybrid mode. This event will unfurl over two phases namely: Phase 1 during January 2023 and Phase 2 during March 2023. Hackoverflow 2.0 is a grand technological spectacle which will be a confluence of innovation and technology. In light of the **G20 summit** to be held in Delhi in 2023, we aim to conduct the operation of the hackathon under the shared umbrella goals and spirit of the Summit. Our primary, governing objective behind this event is to present a platform to young engineers to shape their ingenuity into reality. The **top 20 teams** would get the exclusive opportunity to get fast-tracked to the final round of the upcoming G20 Hackathon.

Our hackathon provides innovative problem statements in accordance with the theme of **“Technologies for Sustainable Development”**. We look forward to seeing the birth of innovative AI based solutions that are in tandem with sustainable technology. We urge you to brainstorm and develop technically adept prototypes that hold the potential to solve these pressing real world problems. Your submissions will be evaluated based on factors including impact, creativity, originality and feasibility.

This zestful celebration would be loaded with offline heuristic workshops and enlightening technical sessions delivered by field specialists to prime you for an intense 48-hour development period supplemented with unremitting guidance from domain experts to felicitously assist you in maneuvering your way to the shortlisting round, finally leading to the ultimate showdown of intelligence, ingenuity, and innovation!

name: Hackanova 2.0
desc:
## Overview

Thakur College of Engineering & Technology is pleased to announce the 2nd edition of **Hackanova**, our most awaited technical event. TCET's Hackanova aims at holding hackathons on the social themes and building their solutions through technology, spreading an endless technical exposure.
The theme of Hackanova 2.0 is **Technology for the Social Good.**

## Timeline

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/36fbc942833c4a39989fe8f111bd88ed/182f5f03-5471-4807-8f1d-957315c84005.png)


## Problem Statements
**You can check out the Problem Statements here:**
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sYayvcTCnxmmemVYOVpqm-2K3_9r7txa/view?usp=sharing


## How to Apply
* Your Idea should be based on the problem statements which will be released by the Hackanova 2.0 Organizing team.
* Use the [Idea Submission Template](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1GoVRMfhw8Aew31h3YA6L76vGGOMeqN1M/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106299849577897965203&rtpof=true&sd=true) to prepare a PPT for your idea.
* Visit https://hackanova2.devfolio.co , sign in and register by filling in your details.
* All team members must upload the same PPT to the application form.
* The team leader should **Create a Team** and share the invite code with their team mates.
* All the TCET students need to additionally fill this form to complete your registration - https://forms.gle/T3dK9D3JtHejLtnP6
* Once all team members have joined they can submit their application.

**Note**: Individual applications and any PPT submissions which are not relevant to the problem statements provided by the Hackanova 2.0 team will be rejected.


## Contact Us
* Join our official discord channel for any queries: https://discord.gg/kwFJZsYnHK

name: SheBuilds
desc:
## About
Our mission is to **encourage fresh hackers** and students to open their minds and think about the various **possibilities technology offers** and shape their ideas for a better world.

**SheBuilds** is a 48-hour gender-focused hackathon with endless creativity. Students are challenged to further what they know by creating projects following their passions. Spending time on projects outside the classroom is the best way to learn what you love and find new interests. In a universe of infinite possibilities, you have 48 hours to innovate and show us what you've got!

## Themes
We have the following themes on which the hackers can work on :
- Healthcare
- Women Empowerment
- Education
- Sustainability
- Blockchain
- AI/ML 

There are no restrictions on ideas and apart from these themes, we are open to any kind of project you want to work on.

More details can be found on our [website here](https://www.shebuilds.tech/)

## Rules
- Follow the [Code of Conduct](https://devfolio.co/code-of-conduct)

prizes.name: FOSS Track
prizes.desc:
*Eligibility*
To receive the prize money, any Indian national who has a valid bank account.

**What you can work on**
A new FOSS app, tool, or library.
An alternative to any existing popular app or service.
Extending and improve an existing project or library.
Design projects: Redesign of an existing FOSS application.
Open hardware.

What you should (probably) not work on
An app or project that extensively uses proprietary service or API.
Yet another Keras model on available datasets.
A simple CRUD application.

**Evaluation**
**License**: Must have a valid Free and Open Source license.
**Communication**: A well written README and video demo are important. These will determine the first round of elimination. Before your code is reviewed, the quality of your README will be. Please be concise in explaining what your project does, how to install it, test it, and use it. Similarly, write concise and meaningful commit messages that show the progression of the project.
**Completeness**: Applications must be complete and working.
**Design and aesthetics**: If you are making a user interface, try and ensure that they are clean, modern, and usable.
**Timeframe**: The project must be reasonably built within the given timeframe. The judgement of the jury will be final in this.
**Credits**: If you are using existing code, make sure you credit it. Plagiarism, which is all too common unfortunately, is strictly not appreciated.
**Demo Video**: Participants must submit a video demo before the clock ends (uploaded on YouTube or any other platform that is accessible to us). Restricted to 3 mins.

prizes.name: FOSS track
prizes.desc:
**Eligibility**
To receive the prize money, any Indian national who has a valid bank account.

**What you can work on**
A new FOSS app, tool, or library.
An alternative to any existing popular app or service.
Extending and improve an existing project or library.
Design projects: Redesign of an existing FOSS application.
Open hardware.

**What you should (probably) not work on**
An app or project that extensively uses proprietary service or API.
Yet another Keras model on available datasets.
A simple CRUD application.

**Evaluation**
**License**: Must have a valid Free and Open Source license.
**Communication**: A well written README and video demo are important. These will determine the first round of elimination. Before your code is reviewed, the quality of your README will be. Please be concise in explaining what your project does, how to install it, test it, and use it. Similarly, write concise and meaningful commit messages that show the progression of the project.
**Completeness**: Applications must be complete and working.
**Design and aesthetics**: If you are making a user interface, try and ensure that they are clean, modern, and usable.
**Timeframe**: The project must be reasonably built within the given timeframe. The judgement of the jury will be final in this.
**Credits**: If you are using existing code, make sure you credit it. Plagiarism, which is all too common unfortunately, is strictly not appreciated.
**Demo Video**: Participants must submit a video demo before the clock ends (uploaded on YouTube or any other platform that is accessible to us). Restricted to 3 mins.

name: Ethos - IIT Guwahati
desc:
Conducted by IIT Guwahati, Ethos is set to be a unique hackathon with a culmination of the rich traditions of the North East with the technical potential of the region. 

Ethos is a way for people all across India to take a crack at solving real-world problems. With problems from the *government of Assam,* you will get a chance to solve genuine issues faced in the North East. Along with the competition, at IIT Guwahati, you will get to explore the beautiful campus, connect with people from all over India, and attend talks by industry leaders.

# Structure

- The Problem Statements will be released soon, and you have to submit an initial presentation of your ideation for the Round 1. You can checkout the problem statements on our website, [here](www.ethosiitg.com). We will release a Google Form for you to submit your presentations on 23rd December.

- Then, results will be announced within a two days of the submission deadline, for the shortlisted candidates who will compete in the final round.

- The final round will be held on 7-8th January 2023 on IIT Guwahati campus, where you will need to submit the complete code solution.

**Join our Discord Server for further communication: https://discord.gg/coding-club-iit-guwahati-789762572512395265**

> Whether you're writing your first line of code, playing around with APIs, or building the next blockchain, Ethos is the place for you. 
*We'll see you soon, right here at IIT Guwahati, this January.*

Note: The nature of final round (fully offline or hybrid) is subject to administrative decisions by the institute. We will make sure to inform well in advance about whatever decision is taken.

name: Oracle of Delphi
desc:
Oracle of Delphi is an AI/ML hackathon which is a part of Enyugma, an annual Techno-Cultural fest organized by IIIT Bhagalpur where developers all over India compete trying to get the highest accuracy on provided datasets.

Link for accessing the datasets:-
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XSRkNYu7958ESknaj6yiDI0G5XmWfrvB?usp=share_link


Guidelines-:
1.	This Hackathon is open to all college/school students.

2.	This is a team challenge. The minimum team size is 1 and max is 3.
3.	The problem statement will be revealed on the day of the hackathon and the dataset could be from the field of Finance, Medical, Business, Environmental Science etc.
4.	The submission will be evaluated automatically.
5.	Participants need to train the model on the provided dataset (obtained from the drive link) and predict on the test dataset given(obtained from the drive link).
6.	The final submission must be in the form of submission.zip file which contains a submission.csv file(which contains predicted target variable) and the source code(ipynb notebook ).
7.	The source code should be written in Python language.

8.	Any publicly available tool or library can be used in the competition.
9.	Use of any external dataset is prohibited and will lead to disqualification.
10.	Any act of cheating or plagiarism will lead to disqualification.
11.	The intellectual property of code/product will belong to IIIT Bhagalpur.
12.	Hackathon organizers reserve the right to amend the rules at any time.
13.	A google form will be released in middle of the hackathon, active participants have to fill the form and mandatory mid-term meet up will be organized.
14.	Winners will be evaluated on averaged out F1 score.
15.	In case of tie the participants will be evaluated in the following order of-: Accuracy, Precision, Quality Of Code and Time of Submission.
16.	Only one submission should be made by individual participant/team.

Our Fest Website-: https://enyugma.iiitbh.ac.in/eventDetail/eventabout.html?search=Oracle%20of%20Delphi

name: GDSC IIIT Delhi Bootcamp
desc:
# Overview
Hello Everyone!
GDSC IIITD is excited to announce Web-Dev Bootcamp, a web development fiesta that brings forth a valuable learning experience for all. This is a 4-day long event which will introduce the basics of web-development along with UI/UX covering everything from the basics of UI creation, to HTML and CSS, to making your first interactive react webpage.
The workshop will be followed by a hackathon, where you will get a chance to show-off these newfound skills to solve some real life problems together.

# # Workshop Outline
Day 1: UI Principles and Hands-on with Figma
Day 2: Introduction to Github, Web Development and React
Day 3: Introduction to HTML and CSS
Day 4: React Deep Dive and Challenge Statement for Hackathon
Check the events sections for more updates.

No prior web-dev experience..? Don’t worry we’ve got you covered!
This is a no-prerequisite event so just coming along with a laptop and a zeal to learn shall be good enough. Highly recommended  for freshers and everyone who wants to get started with Web Development.

Not to forget the exciting prizes, potential internship opportunities, and loads of fun lined up!

A **36 hour national-level Hackathon** organized by **Ramaiah Institute of Technology**, for students and industry professionals, in association with top companies.

**Note : Individual submissions will not be considered**


# Timeline

prizes.desc:
* License: Must have a valid Free and Open Source license.
*Communication: A well written README and video demo are important. These will determine the first round of elimination. Before your code is reviewed, the quality of your README will be. Please be concise in explaining what your project does, how to install it, test it, and use it. Similarly, write concise and meaningful commit messages that show the progression of the project.
* Completeness: Applications must be complete and working.
* Design and aesthetics: If you are making a user interface, try and ensure that they are clean, modern, and usable.
* Timeframe: The project must be reasonably built within the given timeframe. The judgement of the jury will be final in this.
* Credits: If you are using existing code, make sure you credit it. Plagiarism, which is all too common unfortunately, is strictly not appreciated.
* Demo Video: Participants must submit a video demo before the clock ends (uploaded on YouTube or any other platform that is accessible to us). Restricted to 3 mins.

prizes.name: Tezos
prizes.desc:
**Beginner**
* Build a platform for the users to design their own avatar (e.g. https://avatarmaker.com/) and mint them as an NFT on Tezos for a price based on the amount of personalization they’ve added to their avatar such as makeup, hair, facial hair, and accessories, etc.  A generative NFT collection in short. 

**Intermediate**
* Build an on-chain project showcasing platform such as https://producthunt.com, where builders can mint their project as an NFT, and users/audience can show their support to them by upvoting/adding funds to them in form of XTZ for which they can mint a gratitude NFT sort of. (Optional) Implement a leaderboard for the projects too which will get updated by the number of upvotes a project has, i.e. project with the most upvotes/donations will lead the board. 

**Advanced**
* Build a platform to fractionalize a user’s existing NFTs or mint new ones from scratch thus enabling collective ownership of an NFT rather than each person buying their own version. Also add a governance mechanism for the holders of fractions to vote on any related propositions to the NFT such as when to sell, whom to sell etc. Price of each fraction can be proportional to the current floor price of the original edition. Think of fractional.art but on Tezos.

prizes.name: Phala Network
prizes.desc:
# Introduction

On this page, you will find everything you need to participate in the Phala bounties in the Unblock Hackathon event.

Phala Network is a Kusama/Polakdot parachain focusing on trustless cloud computing, based on Secure Enclave technology. Unlike conventional smart contracts, Phala Phat Contracts can:

- be privacy-preserving: you can store secret data like private keys, API keys, or privacy data in a contract;
- interact with HTTP services: you can build an Oracle or Telegram bot as a Fat Contract;
- run computation extensive code: you can build games and analytics jobs in Fat Contracts without block latency.
- connect to Key-Value DB: you can connect to storages like S3, 4EVERLAND, IPFS, Arweave to store information off-chain through HTTPS Requests

# Dates

- Start Hacking: 2022-11-25
- Duration: 7 days
- End of Hackathon: 2022-12-1
- Announcement of Winners: TBD

# Dev Resources

- [Phala Hackathon Submission Repo](https://github.com/Phala-Network/Unblock-Hackathon-2022/issues)
- [Phala Wiki](https://wiki.phala.network/en-us/build/general/intro/)
- [Phat Contracts UI](https://phat.phala.network/)
- [Phala Network GitHub](https://github.com/Phala-Network)
- [Awesome Phat Contracts](https://github.com/Phala-Network/awesome-phat-contracts)
- [Dev Phase](https://github.com/l00k/devphase) - Development tool provided from a community contribution
- Ideas from [previous Hackathon Submissions](https://github.com/Phala-Network/Encode-Hackathon-2021/issues/21)
-Codebase
    -[phala-blockchain](https://github.com/Phala-Network/phala-blockchain)
    -[JS SDK Examples](https://github.com/Phala-Network/js-sdk/tree/main/packages/example)
    -[JS SDK Readme](https://github.com/Phala-Network/js-sdk/tree/main/packages/sdk)


# Hackathon Bounties:

**Challenge #1 - Reward 500 PHA for the first 50 Submissions**

Complete the [Oracle Workshop](https://github.com/Phala-Network/oracle-workshop) steps for the Beginner and Advanced Challenge. Phat Contracts are different from the typical EVM Smart Contract. In contrast, Phat Contracts are written in the Rust-based eDSL [ink!](https://paritytech.github.io/ink/) and compiled down to WASM. Walking through this workshop and getting some hands on experience here will show you the basics of building an Oracle with cross-contract calls that can be valuable for entering into Challenge #2.

**Challenge #2 - Rewards: 1st - 10000 PHA; 2nd - 7000 PHA; 3rd - 3500 PHA; 800 PHA for Qualified Submissions**

Build a fully functional dApp with Phat Contract on Phala Testnet.

A qualified dApp should be useful to solve some real-world problems or bring fun to people. It should also utilize the unique features of Phala (privacy-preserving, computation-intensive, or with HTTPS requests).

**In addition, documentation and tutorial contributions are elegible to our [Bounty Program](https://github.com/Phala-Network/bounty-program).**

The contribution can be:

-Fixes or improvements on our [wiki repo](https://github.com/Phala-Network/phala-wiki-next)
-Published video tutorials on Youtube and Twitter (please submit an issue in the Code Bounty Program repo)
-Documentation or bug fixes in our [main repo](https://github.com/Phala-Network/phala-blockchain) or [JS SDK](https://github.com/Phala-Network/js-sdk)

# Chat and Support

Meet friends and the Phala team at our [Official Discord Server](https://discord.com/invite/nJaehCD98Y)!

If you have any questions about the hackathon, Phala development, or you want to report a bug, we have a **#hackathon** group dedicated to that.

# About Phala Network

[Phala Network](https://phala.network/) is a Web3.0 computing cloud that supports data privacy while remaining trustless. Unlike centralized cloud service, Phala doesn’t own any server or data center. Anyone can provide permissionless servers into Phala Network, and because of a clever combination of blockchain and secure enclave, we can make sure the servers can’t be evil even when they are in an edge network situation. Together, this creates the infrastructure for a powerful, secure, and scalable trustless computing cloud.

# Some useful resources include:

- [Main page](https://phala.network/)
- [Phala Wiki](https://wiki.phala.network/en-us/build/general/intro/) about Phala applications, mining and Phat Contract development
- [Discord channel](https://discord.gg/myBmQu5) and [Forum](https://forum.phala.network/) to discuss with us and our community members directly
- [Medium](https://medium.com/phala-network) and [Twitter](https://twitter.com/PhalaNetwork) to learn about our latest progress

name: Solana HackDay Delhi
tagline: A 12-hours Hackathon to Learn, Buidl, and Earn on Solana
desc:
**Solana x SuperteamDAO** brings you HackDay, a series **of 12-hour hackathons** for students, where you can learn, build, and ship a project on Solana with a prize pool of $1000+!

At HackDay Delhi, you can expect a 12-hour-long experience of coding, learning, networking, and having fun.

While you work towards building any project you want to, you will be complemented with informative workshops, enjoyable mini-games, cool prizes, and pizzas to eat. 😎

The hackathon is open to all kinds of projects across themes, but here are a few things we’re actively thinking about these days in case you’re looking for some inspiration:

1. **Promote Decentralization.** Create developer tooling and community projects focussed on promoting and bringing more decentralization to Solana as well as the world at large.

2. **DAO Tooling:** Create coordination, communication, and payment tools for communities using Solana as the backbone of their infrastructure.

3. **Developer Tooling**: Create tools, programs, and hacks, making it easier and faster for engineers to build the next generation of dApps on Solana.

4. **Consumer Payments**: Build payments apps for consumers and businesses, making P2P payments, as well as commerce better integrated with the crypto ecosystem using Solana Pay.

5. **Streaming Payments**: Make apps using Streamflow or similar protocols to make payroll, commerce, content, and subscription management platforms that make users feel the full magic of streaming payments.

6. **Cause-driven building:** We’re also looking to fund projects and research around using crypto to create a more inclusive financial system and innovative solutions towards climate change.

You can find a list of project ideas for builders free to explore [here](https://solana.com/summercamp/ideas).

> If you're new to Solana, you can start learning with our [Solana Core](https://buildspace.so/solana-core) course and ship a project during the hackathon!

**Event Summary:**

**Day and Date:** Saturday, 19th November 2022
**Timings:** 08:00 AM - 10:00 PM
**Venue:** [C101, First Floor, Lecture Hall Complex, IIIT Delhi](https://goo.gl/maps/2dJB6tmaZ76StqQf8)

*A big thanks to IEEE IIITD Student Branch for helping us out with the venue!*
